DAMGHANI:v1p20/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p20/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p20/r2.claim: Akhadha can mean acceptance: accepting a covenant, a proposed judgment, alms, or pardon, and accepting a ransom is denied in the cited passage.

DAMGHANI:v1p299/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r1.claim: Purification can mean cleansing people of sins.
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r1.anchor: تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها يعني تطهرهم من الذنوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r1.claim: The address is to the Prophet and its pronoun refers to the repentant latecomers; they offer their wealth and ask him to purify them, but he says he was not ordered to take it until this verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r1.anchor: الخطاب للرسول، والضمير عائد على الذين خلطوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet took one-third of their property in response to ‘take from their wealth.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r2.anchor: فيروى أنه أخذ ثلث أموالهم مراعاة لقوله: خذ من أموالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r3.claim: Most early interpreters place the verse among the repentant stragglers; a group of jurists instead reads it as the obligatory zakāt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r3.anchor: والذي تظاهرت به أقوال المتأولين ابن عباس وغيره: أنها في هؤلاء المتخلفين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r4.claim: On the zakāt reading, ‘their wealth’ means zakatable assets generally, excluding houses and clothing, and no fixed amount is specified, so even a small voluntary amount can count.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r4.anchor: إذ يخرج عنه الأموال التي لا زكاة فيها كالرباع والثياب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r5.claim: The command ‘take’ indicates that the imam is responsible for collecting and administering alms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r5.anchor: وفي قوله: خذ، دليل على أن الإمام هو الذي يتولى أخذ الصدقات وينظر فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r6.claim: He parses ‘from their wealth’ with ‘take’; ‘purifying them’ can be a circumstantial clause whose subject is the implied subject of ‘take,’ among other parses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r6.anchor: ومن أموالهم: متعلق بخذ وتطهرهم، وتزكيهم حال من ضمير خذ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r7.claim: He rejects making ‘purifying them’ modify charity while ‘you purify’ is a separate circumstance unless an implied subject is supplied; that construction is rare.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r7.anchor: وهذا فاسد المعنى، ولو كان بغير واو جاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r8.claim: Purification may mean intensified cleansing, or growth and blessing in wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r8.anchor: والتزكية مبالغة في التطهر وزيادة فيه، أو بمعنى الإنماء والبركة في المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb in a causative form as another way to express purification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: تطهرهم من أطهر واطهر وطهر للتعدية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r10.claim: ‘Pray for them’ may mean supplicate, ask forgiveness, or perform funeral prayer for them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r10.anchor: وصل عليهم أي ادع لهم، أو استغفر لهم، أو صل عليهم إذا ماتوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the Prophet’s prayer as reassurance that God accepted their charity; he also reports meanings of mercy and nearness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r11.anchor: قاله: ابن عباس. أو رحمة لهم قاله أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r12.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r12.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet’s prayer gives them increased dignity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r12.anchor: أو زيادة وقار لهم قاله: قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda understands ‘sakan’ as strengthening their hearts; other glosses include security.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p499/r13.anchor: أو تثبيت لقلوبهم قاله: أبو عبيدة، أو أمن لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r1.claim: The cited poem uses ‘sakan’ in the sense of shelter or comfort; the several glosses are close in meaning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī gives a philosophical account: the Prophet’s radiant soul affects the repentants’ souls through prayer, clarifying and elevating them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r2.anchor: لأن روحه صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت روحا قوية مشرقة صافية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r3.speaker: ابن النقيب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r3.claim: Ibn al-Naqīb rejects al-Rāzī’s explanation as philosophical and incompatible with the method of Qur’anic exegesis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r3.anchor: كلام الرازي كلام فلسفي يشير فيه إلى أن قوى الأنفس مؤثرة فعالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say the repentants from whom charity was taken were distinct from the three whose case was deferred.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: في هؤلاء المعترفين المأخوذ منهم الصدقة هم سوى الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r5.claim: Two canonical readers and Ḥafṣ read ‘your prayer’ in the singular here and at Hūd 11:87; the rest read the plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وحفص: إن صلاتك هنا، وفي هود صلاتك بالتوحيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r6.claim: God hears their confession and knows their remorse and repentance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p500/r6.anchor: والله سميع باعترافهم، عليم بندامتهم وتوبتهم

DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.claim: Seven stayed behind at Tabuk; four mixed good and bad deeds—Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubaba, Haram, and Aws—and they were pardoned and ordered to give charity.
DURR-FULL:v4p277/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} قال: ذكر لنا أنهم كانوا سبعة رهط

STUDYQURAN:9:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:intro/r7.claim: Rules for zakāh and charitable giving are prominent themes.
STUDYQURAN:9:intro/r7.anchor: The rules governing the zakāh, or alms, and the giving of charity also figure prominently in this sūrah (vv. 58–60, 103–4)

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r1.claim: A report connects the verse with the repentant men of 9:102: after they offered their wealth, the Prophet initially said he had not been commanded to accept it; revelation then directed them to give a third as expiation.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r1.anchor: It is said that this verse was revealed in connection with the repentant men of v. 102

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r2.claim: Some Arabian tribes after the Prophet's death used this interpretation to argue that alms were owed only to him personally and refused to give them to Abū Bakr.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r2.anchor: those Arabian tribes who believed that alms were only owed to the Prophet personally for him to distribute

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r3.claim: On the first interpretation, the charitable offering is expiation charity.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r3.anchor: According to this interpretation, the charitable offering refers to the charity of expiation

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r4.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r4.claim: The other main opinion takes the offering as institutional obligatory alms, usually called zakāh.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r4.anchor: this verse refers to the institutional alms

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r5.claim: This verse cannot restrict obligatory alms to payments made directly to the Prophet, since other verses specify recipients such as the poor, indigent, beggar, and deprived.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r5.anchor: This verse could not, it is argued, be the basis for restricting obligatory alms to those given directly to the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r6.claim: The Quran also describes messengers as purifying people, often together with teaching the Book and imparting knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r6.anchor: The purification of a people by a messenger is also mentioned

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r7.claim: Giving charity purifies a person from the defilement of sin and disobedience to God.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r7.anchor: The giving of charity purifies one from the defilement of sin and disobedience to God

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r8.claim: The commentary refers the meaning of blessings to its discussions at 2:3, 9:99, and 33:56.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r8.anchor: On the meaning of the blessings

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r9.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r9.claim: It is said that the Prophet would pray, O God, bless them, when people brought charity for distribution to the community.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r9.anchor: when someone brought charity to the Prophet for distribution to the community, he would pray, “O God, bless them

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r10.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r10.claim: The Prophet's blessings comfort people because hearing his prayers makes them glad and God's response brings peace to their hearts.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r10.anchor: when people heard the Prophet’s prayers, they became glad and, as a result of God’s Response to his prayers, found peace in their hearts

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r11.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r11.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet's blessings are a mercy for the people.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r11.anchor: his blessings were a mercy for them

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r12.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r12.claim: Many hold that this form of blessing is restricted to the Prophet: Muslims invoke blessings only on him, and only he may bless others.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r12.anchor: Many say that the act of blessing in this particular way is reserved only for the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r13.speaker: al-Rāzī and al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r13.claim: Al-Rāzī and al-Qurṭubī reject restricting this form of blessing to the Prophet because he is an exemplar for all actions.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r13.anchor: Al-Rāzī and al-Qurṭubī, however, are of the opinion that there is no reason why this particular form of invoking blessings should be restricted to the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:9:103/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r14.claim: Muslims invoke blessings and peace upon Muhammad in prayer and when his name is mentioned, but invoke only peace for other prophets.
STUDYQURAN:9:103/r14.anchor: Muslims invoke blessings and peace upon the Prophet Muhammad in prayers and also when his name is mentioned, while only peace is invoked in the case of other prophets

TAB-FULL:v11p579/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r4.speaker: ثعلبة بن حاطب الأنصاري
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r4.claim: When collectors came, Thalaba called the alms a tax, while a man of Sulaym willingly gave his best camels; the report connects this episode to the revelation of 9:103.
TAB-FULL:v11p579/r4.anchor: فخرجا حتى أتيا ثعلبة، فسألاه الصدقة، وأقرأاه كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r1.claim: The command concerns those who confessed their sins and repented: their alms cleanse them from the stain of their sins.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r1.anchor: وتنميهم وترفعهم عن خسيس منازل أهل النفاق بها، إلى منازل أهل الإخلاص

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r2.claim: The alms grow and elevate them from the low station of hypocrites to the station of the sincere.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r2.anchor: وتنميهم وترفعهم عن خسيس منازل أهل النفاق بها، إلى منازل أهل الإخلاص

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r3.claim: To pray for them means to ask God to forgive their sins.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r3.anchor: وادع لهم بالمغفرة لذنوبهم، واستغفر لهم منها

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r4.claim: The Prophet's prayer and request for forgiveness reassure the penitents that God has pardoned them and accepted their repentance.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r4.anchor: إن دعاءك واستغفارك طمأنينة لهم بأن الله قد عفا عنهم وقبل توبتهم

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r5.claim: God hears the Prophet's prayer and all creatures' speech, and knows what he seeks for them and all other affairs of His servants.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r5.anchor: والله سميع لدعائك إذا دعوت لهم ولغير ذلك من كلام خلقه، عليم بما تطلب بهم بدعائك ربك لهم

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Lubaba and his companions offered their wealth after release, but the Prophet awaited God's command; this verse authorized alms, with purification glossed as obedience and sincerity.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جاءوا بأموالهم يعني أبا لبابة وأصحابه حين أطلقوا فقالوا: يا رسول الله هذه أموالنا

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Lubaba and two companions brought their property, asked the Prophet to give alms on their behalf and pray for their forgiveness; he waited for revelation, then took some of it for charity.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما أطلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا لبابة وصاحبيه

TAB-FULL:v11p661/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that after the Prophet freed Abu Lubaba and those who had tied themselves to the pillars, they offered him charity to purify them and the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v11p661/r8.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، قال: " لما أطلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا لبابة والذين ربطوا أنفسهم بالسواري

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r1.claim: Those who had tied themselves to pillars asked the Prophet to purify their wealth; Sa'id adds that when one of three fell ill, the other two shared the illness, and the two who were his uncles became blind while the last kept praying until he too went blind.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " قال الذين ربطوا أنفسهم بالسواري حين عفا الله عنهم يا نبي الله طهر أموالنا

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the four people addressed as Jad ibn Qays, Abu Lubaba, Haram, and Aws; they had promised to spend, strive, and give charity.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " الأربعة: جد بن قيس، وأبو لبابة، وحرام، وأوس، وهم الذين قيل فيهم

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r3.claim: Qatada glosses sakan as dignity or composure for them.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r3.anchor: حدثنا بشر، قال: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Abu Lubaba and his companions offered wealth for charity and purification after release; the Prophet waited for God's instruction, then followed this command.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، قال: " لما أطلق نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا لبابة وأصحابه

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains praying for them as asking forgiveness for the sins they had committed.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس، قوله: " {خذ من أموالهم صدقة} [التوبة: 103] أبو لبابة وأصحابه. {وصل عليهم}

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the recipients as hypocrites who stayed behind at Tabuk, admitted hypocrisy and doubt, and offered alms as renewed repentance; he links the passage to the prohibition on praying over dead hypocrites.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم}

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r7.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r7.claim: Basran grammarians say the raised verb may begin a clause or describe the alms, with the verb purify repeated for emphasis.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: رفع «تزكيهم بها» في الابتداء وإن شئت جعلته من صفة الصدقة

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r8.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r8.claim: Kufan grammarians prefer the jussive for purify if it refers to the Prophet, since no pronoun returns to alms; if alms purify and the Prophet purifies through them, either verb may be jussive or raised.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: إن كان قوله: {تطهرهم} [التوبة: 103] للنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r9.claim: Al-Tabari prefers taking purify as modifying alms because readers unanimously raise it; he reads and you purify them through it as a new clause, hence its raised form.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: والصواب في ذلك من القول أن قوله: {تطهرهم} [التوبة: 103] من صلة «الصدقة»

TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r10.claim: One reported interpretation glosses the Prophet's prayer as mercy for the recipients.
TAB-FULL:v11p661#2/r10.anchor: فقال بعضهم: رحمة لهم. ذكر من قال ذلك

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the Prophet's prayer as mercy for the recipients.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {إن صلاتك سكن لهم} [التوبة: 103] يقول: رحمة لهم

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the Prophet's prayer as dignity or composure for the recipients.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {إن صلاتك سكن لهم} [التوبة: 103] أي وقار لهم

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r3.speaker: قراء المدينة
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r3.claim: Medinan readers use the plural reading salawatuka, meaning your prayers or supplications.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r3.anchor: فقرأته قراء المدينة: «إن صلواتك سكن لهم» بمعنى دعواتك

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r4.speaker: قراء العراق وبعض المكيين
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r4.claim: Readers in Iraq and some Meccan readers use the singular reading salatuka, meaning your prayer or supplication.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r4.anchor: وقرأ قراء العراق وبعض المكيين: {إن صلاتك سكن لهم} [التوبة: 103] بمعنى إن دعاءك

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r5.speaker: قراء التوحيد
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r5.claim: Readers favoring the singular argued that it carries a collective and larger-number sense, whereas plural salawat denotes a count from three to ten.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r5.anchor: وكأن الذين قرءوا ذلك على التوحيد رأوا أن قراءته بالتوحيد أصح؛ لأن في التوحيد من معنى الجمع وكثرة العدد

TAB-FULL:v11p663/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the singular because the verse reports the Prophet's prayer as reassurance for the people, not how many prayers he offered; he does not rely on the numerical rationale.
TAB-FULL:v11p663/r6.anchor: وبالتوحيد عندنا القراءة لا لعلة أن ذلك في العدد أكثر من الصلوات، ولكن المقصود منه الخبر عن دعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r4.claim: Purification removes dirt and defilement so a thing becomes clear and ready for growth and the appearance of its effects and blessings.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r4.anchor: التطهير إزالة الأوساخ والقذارات من الشيء ليصفى وجوده ويستعد للنشوء والنماء

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r5.claim: Tazkiya means growth and guidance through the arrival of good and the appearance of blessings, like pruning a tree to improve its growth and fruit.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r5.anchor: والتزكية إنماؤه وإعطاء الرشد له بلحوق الخيرات وظهور البركات كالشجرة بقطع الزوائد

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r6.claim: Combining purification and growth is an especially subtle expression, joining removal of impediments with flourishing.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r6.anchor: فالجمع بين التطهير والتزكية في الآية من لطيف التعبير

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r7.claim: The plural 'their properties' signals that the charity is taken from different kinds of wealth: gold and silver, camels, cattle and sheep, and wheat, barley, dates and raisins.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r7.anchor: ولم يقل من مالهم ليكون إشارة إلى أنها مأخوذة من أصناف المال، وهي النقدان الذهب والفضة

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r8.claim: The verbs address the Prophet, rather than describe the charity itself: the pronoun in 'by it' refers to charity, meaning he purifies and develops them through taking it.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r8.anchor: وليس وصفا لحال الصدقة، والدليل عليه ضمير بها الراجع إلى الصدقة أي خذ يا محمد

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r9.claim: Praying for donors means supplicating for good and blessing for them and their property, as the Prophet's established practice shows.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r9.anchor: الصلاة عليهم هي الدعاء لهم والسياق يفيد أنه دعاء لهم ولأموالهم بالخير والبركة

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r10.claim: The donors' souls find reassurance and trust in the Prophet's prayer; it also thanks them for their service to God.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r10.anchor: المراد به أن نفوسهم تسكن إلى دعائك وتثق به وهو نوع شكر لسعيهم في الله

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r11.claim: The closing assurance that God hears and knows likewise reassures those charged with religious duties who hear or recite the verse.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r11.anchor: سكن يسكن إليه نفوس المكلفين ممن يسمع الآية أو يتلوها

TABATABAI:9:102-104/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r12.claim: The verse establishes financial zakat as an obligation and one of the pillars of the religious law; abundant reports from the Imams of the Prophet's family and others explain it this way.
TABATABAI:9:102-104/r12.anchor: والآية تتضمن حكم الزكاة المالية التي هي من أركان الشريعة والملة على ما هو ظاهر الآية

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r2.claim: Other reports differ over the men's names and say the charity verse concerned their specific wealth; the author considers that account weak because many reports show the verse concerns obligatory zakat.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r2.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى روايات أخرى رواها في الدر المنثور بينها اختلاف في أسامي الرجال

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r3.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about Abū Lubāba alone, after he told Banū Qurayẓa that surrendering to the Prophet's judgment meant slaughter.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r3.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر الباقر عليه السلام أنها نزلت في أبي لبابة ولم يذكر غيره معه

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Sinān reports from Imam al-Ṣādiq that in Ramadan the Prophet announced zakat as obligatory like prayer, specifying gold, silver, camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates and raisins, and exempting other property.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r4.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن عبد الله بن سنان قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام لما نزلت هذه الآية { خذ من أموالهم صدقة

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r5.claim: The same report says no further wealth obligation was imposed until a year had passed; after the first Ramadan fast, the Prophet's caller urged Muslims to purify their wealth so their prayers would be accepted, and collectors were dispatched.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r5.anchor: ثم لم يفرض لشيء من أموالهم حتى حال عليه الحول من قابل فصاموا وأفطروا

TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r6.claim: Ibn Abī Awfā reports that when someone brought charity the Prophet prayed for that person's family; when Ibn Abī Awfā's father brought his charity, he prayed for the family of Abī Awfā.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#4/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتي بصدقة قال اللهم صل على آل فلان

TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r1.claim: Islam assigns society a share in wealth's benefits through obligations such as zakat and khums; this answers society's need for resources and resembles provisions in earlier law codes and customary systems.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r1.anchor: وقد عزلت الشريعة الإسلامية سهما من منافع الأموال وفوائدها للمجتمع كالصدقة الواجبة التي هي الزكاة وكالخمس

TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r2.claim: The first distinctive feature is that zakat and similar shares attach when new wealth arises, such as harvest or trading profit, and the remaining shares belong to the owner or worker.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r2.anchor: أنها اقتصرت في وضع هذا النوع من الجهات المالية على كينونة الملك وحدوثه موجودا ولم يتعد ذلك

TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r3.claim: He suggests 2:29 and 4:5 may imply that newly arising wealth first belongs wholly to society, after which a share is assigned to the individual; zakat or khums remains society's share, while the individual owns the rest.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r3.anchor: خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا

TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r4.claim: Once ownership has settled, Islam imposes no further claim on the owner's property merely because of conditions or circumstances; charges on persons, land or commerce at special times are treated as usurpation, except emergencies threatening society's survival.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#5/r4.anchor: وأما إذا انعقد الملك واستقر لمالكه فلا اعتراض لمعترض على مالك في حال أو عند شرط

TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r1.claim: The second feature favors individuals in distributing public shares: zakat has eight categories, only one for God's cause, while the others serve people; khums has six shares, with five assigned to the Prophet, kin, orphans, needy and travelers.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r1.anchor: فإنه يجعل السهام في الزكاة ثمانية لا يختص بسبيل الله منها إلا سهم واحد وباقي السهام للأفراد

TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r2.claim: Because individuals are society's constituent elements, reducing class differences and balancing social forces requires improving individuals and bringing their circumstances closer; spending communal wealth on prestige projects while rich and poor diverge does not solve social harm.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r2.anchor: وذلك أن الفرد هو العنصر الوحيد لتكون المجتمع، ورفع اختلاف الطبقات الذي هو من أصول برنامج الإسلام

TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r3.claim: Third, a Muslim may in some circumstances pay obligatory zakat directly to eligible poor or needy recipients rather than route it through the ruler or collector.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r3.anchor: أن للفرد من المسلمين أن يصرف ما عليه من الحق المالي الواجب كالزكاة مثلا في بعض أرباب السهام

TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r4.claim: This direct-distribution right reflects the independence Islam grants individuals, like the authority to give safe conduct to hostile non-Muslims; the ruler may prohibit it when public Muslim interests require, and must be obeyed.
TABATABAI:9:97-106#6/r4.anchor: وهذا نوع من الاحترام الاستقلالي الذي اعتبره الإسلام لأفراد مجتمعه نظير إعطاء الذمة

TABRISI:9:103/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
TABRISI:9:103/r1.claim: The Kufan readers except Abu Bakr read “inna salataka” in the singular, as in Hud; the remaining readers use the plural “salawatuka.”
TABRISI:9:103/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر

TABRISI:9:103/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r2.claim: Prayer in Arabic means supplication; al-A'sha's verse uses the verb for a prayer over a wine jar, supporting the command to supplicate for the donors.
TABRISI:9:103/r2.anchor: الصلاة في اللغة الدعاء قال الأعشى

TABRISI:9:103/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r3.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:9:103/r3.claim: Sibawayh treats phrases such as God’s prayer on His messenger and “woe to the defrauders” as descriptions of those deserving the expression, not prayers from God; he applies the same account to related forms.
TABRISI:9:103/r3.anchor: وهذا مذهب سيبويه فإذا كانت الصلاة مصدرا

TABRISI:9:103/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r4.claim: As a verbal noun, “salat” has the same form for singular and plural, like “voice”; when kinds differ it may take a plural, as in the verse about the lowest of voices.
TABRISI:9:103/r4.anchor: فإذا كانت الصلاة مصدرا وقع على الجمع والمفرد

TABRISI:9:103/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r5.claim: Al-Tabrisi rejects the claim that singular salat is for many and plural salawat for few: the feminine plural can denote either, as in the cited verses.
TABRISI:9:103/r5.anchor: فأما من زعم أن الصلاة أولى

TABRISI:9:103/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r6.claim: “Tutahhiruhum” may modify “charity,” with its feminine subject and “bihā” explanatory; or address the Prophet—“you purify them by it”—with the clause still modifying charity.
TABRISI:9:103/r6.anchor: إما أن يكون صفة لصدقة ويكون التاء للتأنيث

TABRISI:9:103/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r7.claim: Unlike “tutahhiruhum,” “tuzakkīhim” can only address the Prophet directly.
TABRISI:9:103/r7.anchor: وأما { وتزكيهم } فلا يكون إلا للخطاب

TABRISI:9:103/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r8.claim: Although “tutahhiruhum” could begin an independent clause, al-Tabrisi prefers connecting it syntactically to what precedes.
TABRISI:9:103/r8.anchor: يجوز أن يكون على الاستئناف وحمله على الاتصال أولى

TABRISI:9:103/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103/r9.claim: “Min” is partitive, since not all wealth must be given; “their wealth” rather than “their property” includes all kinds of assets, generally requiring collection across Muslims’ wealth except where evidence excludes a category.
TABRISI:9:103/r9.anchor: أدخل من للتبعيض لأنه لم يجب

TABRISI:9:103/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r10.speaker: الحسن وغيره
TABRISI:9:103/r10.claim: One view takes the command as a special, intensified penitential charity from these repentant people, not the obligatory zakat.
TABRISI:9:103/r10.anchor: الكفارة للذنوب التي أصابوها عن الحسن وغيره

TABRISI:9:103/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103/r11.speaker: الجبائي وأكثر أهل التفسير
TABRISI:9:103/r11.claim: Al-Jubba'i and most exegetes identify the charity as obligatory zakat, which al-Tabrisi calls the apparent reading absent evidence for restriction; he lists the nisab thresholds for silver, gold, livestock, crops, and fruit.

TABRISI:9:103-104/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103-104/r1.claim: The charity cleanses them of sin, while the Prophet attributes purity to them and prays for their purification; alternatively, both verbs describe what the Prophet does through the charity.

TABRISI:9:103-104/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103-104/r2.claim: God commands the Prophet to pray that those giving charity have it accepted, using a supplication asking God to reward their gift and bless what remains.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r2.anchor: هذا أمر من الله تعالى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:9:103-104/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
TABRISI:9:103-104/r3.claim: The Prophet used to pray for groups bringing charity; Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa brought charity and heard him pray for his family. Al-Bukhari and Muslim include the report in their Sahih collections.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r3.anchor: فأتاه ابن أبي أوفى بصدقة فقال اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى أورده البخاري ومسلم

TABRISI:9:103-104/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103-104/r4.claim: “Sakan” means that the Prophet’s supplications quiet the donors’ souls.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r4.anchor: أي إن دعواتك مما تسكن نفوسهم إليه

TABRISI:9:103-104/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:9:103-104/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “sakan” as mercy for the donors.

TABRISI:9:103-104/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r6.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
TABRISI:9:103-104/r6.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi understand it as assurance and tranquility that God has accepted their charity.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r6.anchor: وقار وطمأنينة لهم أن الله قد قبل منهم عن قتادة والكلبي

TABRISI:9:103-104/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:9:103-104/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses “sakan” as support or confirmation for them.

TABRISI:9:103-104/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103-104/r8.claim: God hears the Prophet’s prayer for them and knows how they handle charity.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r8.anchor: يسمع دعاءك لهم ويعلم ما يكون منهم في الصدقات

TABRISI:9:103-104/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:103-104/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:103-104/r10.claim: The repentant had asked the Prophet to take their wealth as expiation; he waited for divine permission, and God clarifies that acceptance belongs to God, not the Prophet.
TABRISI:9:103-104/r10.anchor: لما سألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يأخذ من أموالهم

THALABI:v5p89/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r4.claim: The commentators say the Messenger took one-third of their wealth and left two-thirds, reasoning that God said take from their wealth, not take their wealth in full.
THALABI:v5p89/r4.anchor: قالوا جميعا: وأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم ثلث أموالهم وترك الإثنين لأن الله عز وجل قال: خذ من أموالهم ولم يقل: أموالهم

THALABI:v5p89/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r6.claim: The transmitted nominative reading is circumstantial, not a response clause: take an alms that purifies them.
THALABI:v5p89/r6.anchor: والقراءة بالرفع حالا لا جوابا، أي خذ من أموالهم صدقة مطهرة

THALABI:v5p89/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r7.claim: The author glosses the alms as purifying and sanctifying the donors.
THALABI:v5p89/r7.anchor: أي خذ من أموالهم صدقة مطهرة ومزكية كقول الحطيئة: متى تأته تعشو

THALABI:v5p89/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r8.speaker: الحطيئة
THALABI:v5p89/r8.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa's poetic line is cited as Arabic usage supporting the sense of the participle مزكية.
THALABI:v5p89/r8.anchor: ومزكية كقول الحطيئة: متى تأته تعشو الى ضوء ناره

THALABI:v5p89/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r9.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب
THALABI:v5p89/r9.claim: Muslima ibn Muḥārib reads both verbs in the jussive as a response to the command.
THALABI:v5p89/r9.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن محارب: تطهرهم وتزكيهم بالجزم على الجواب

THALABI:v5p89/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v5p89/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads تطهرهم with a light initial form, from أَطْهَرَ, and explains تزكيهم as purifying them.
THALABI:v5p89/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: تطهرهم خفيفة من أطهر تطهير وتزكيهم أي تطهرهم

THALABI:v5p89/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r11.claim: One reported interpretation says the alms reform the people.

THALABI:v5p89/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r12.claim: Another interpretation says the alms raise them from the ranks of hypocrites to the ranks of the sincere.
THALABI:v5p89/r12.anchor: وقيل: ترفعهم من منازل المنافقين الى منازل المخلصين

THALABI:v5p89/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r13.claim: Another reported view takes the pronoun to refer to their wealth itself.
THALABI:v5p89/r13.anchor: وقيل: ترفعهم من منازل المنافقين الى منازل المخلصين، وقيل: هي أموالهم

THALABI:v5p89/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p89/r14.claim: Pray for them and ask forgiveness for them; alternatively, the collector says, “May God reward what you gave and bless what you kept.”
THALABI:v5p89/r14.anchor: وصل عليهم أي استغفر لهم وادع لهم، وقيل: هو قول الوالي إذا أخذ الصدقة

THALABI:v5p89/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p89/r15.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p89/r15.claim: The Prophet uses prayer here to mean supplication: when a guest is fasting, he should respond to the invitation and pray for the host.
THALABI:v5p89/r15.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا دعي أحدكم الى طعام فليجبه

THALABI:v5p90/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p90/r1.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse about praying over a wine jar illustrates prayer as a wish for its safety and blessing.

THALABI:v5p90/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p90/r2.claim: A second poetic example uses prayer to mean asking God to protect the speaker's father from illness and pain.
THALABI:v5p90/r2.anchor: يا رب جنب أبي الأوصاب والوجعا

THALABI:v5p90/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r3.speaker: أهل الكوفة
THALABI:v5p90/r3.claim: The Kufans read صلاتك in the singular here and at the cited places in Hūd and al-Muʾminūn.
THALABI:v5p90/r3.anchor: إن صلاتك قرأ أهل الكوفة: صلاتك على الواحد هاهنا وفي سورة هود والمؤمنين

THALABI:v5p90/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v5p90/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayd prefers the singular, transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, because ṣalāh can denote the category of prayers; he distinguishes the singular ritual prayer from plural individual prayers.
THALABI:v5p90/r4.anchor: أبو عبيد قال: لأن الصلاة هي من الصلوات

THALABI:v5p90/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
THALABI:v5p90/r5.claim: The remaining readers use the plural, which Abū Ḥātim prefers; he rejects the claim that the feminine plural is rare because the Qurʾān also pluralizes God's words.
THALABI:v5p90/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون كلها بالجمع واختاره أبو حاتم، قال: ومن زعم أن الصلوات من الصلاة

THALABI:v5p90/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p90/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses their security as mercy for them.
THALABI:v5p90/r6.anchor: سكن لهم قال ابن عباس: رحمة لهم

THALABI:v5p90/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p90/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses their security as dignity and composure for them.
THALABI:v5p90/r7.anchor: سكن لهم قال ابن عباس: رحمة لهم، وقال قتادة: وقار لهم

THALABI:v5p90/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r8.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v5p90/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says it reassures them that God has accepted their repentance.
THALABI:v5p90/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: طمأنينة لهم إن الله قد قبل منهم

THALABI:v5p90/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r9.speaker: معاذ
THALABI:v5p90/r9.claim: Muʿādh says the Prophet's prayer is purification for them.

THALABI:v5p90/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p90/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as steadfastness.
THALABI:v5p90/r10.anchor: وقال معاذ: تزكية لهم منك، أبو عبيدة: تثبيت

THALABI:v5p90/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r11.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p90/r11.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā, a participant in the tree pledge, reports that the Prophet prayed for those who brought alms and said, “O God, bless Abū Awfā,” when he brought his own.
THALABI:v5p90/r11.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى، وكان من أصحاب الشجرة: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه قوم بصدقاتهم

THALABI:v5p90/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p90/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the alms in this episode were voluntary expiation, not obligatory zakat.
THALABI:v5p90/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ليس هذا صدقة الفرض

THALABI:v5p90/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p90/r13.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v5p90/r13.claim: ʿIkrima instead says the alms were obligatory zakat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r1.claim: After the Prophet excused and released these people, they offered the wealth that had kept them behind and asked him to give it as charity, purify them, and seek forgiveness; he said he had not been ordered to take anything, then the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: (لما عذر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هؤلاء وأطلقهم قالوا: يا رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r2.claim: The Prophet took one third of their wealth and left two thirds, reasoning from the command to take from their wealth rather than all of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r2.anchor: فأخذ رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ثلث أموالهم وترك الثلثين؛ لأن الله تعالى قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r3.claim: This charity expiates their sins and is not the obligatory alms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r3.anchor: قال الحسن: (هذه الصدقة هي كفارة الذنوب التي أصابوها وليست بالزكاة المفروضة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r4.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r4.claim: Ibn Kaysan gives the same view as al-Hasan: the charity is expiation rather than obligatory alms.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r5.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r5.claim: Ikrima says the charity is the obligatory alms.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r6.speaker: أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r6.claim: Although the verse was revealed about voluntary charity, its legal ruling is general.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r6.anchor: وقال أهل العلم: (الآية وإن كانت نازلة في صدقة التطوع، فهي عامة الحكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r7.claim: The imam has stronger right to collect charities; the plural wealth implies taking some from each category: crops, livestock, and money.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r7.anchor: ومعنى الجمع في الأموال يقتضي أنه يأخذ بعض كل صنف من المال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r8.claim: The charity purifies them from sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: تطهرهم من الذنوب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows the verb to describe the charity, but prefers it to address the Prophet: take charity and thereby purify them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r9.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (يصلح (¬3) أن يكون: {تطهرهم} [نعتا للصدقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r10.claim: If the verb refers to the charity, taking it removes people's moral refuse, so its removal is purification.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: (من جعل (التاء) في {تطهرهم} ضمير الصدقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r11.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r11.claim: Purification can mean a legal status, not removal of bodily filth, just as polytheists are legally called impure in 9:28.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن # تكون طهارة من جهة الحكم وإن لم تزل شيئا نجسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r12.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r12.claim: If the first verb describes the charity, the following phrase can be detached and read as the collector's action: you purify them with it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه في {تطهرهم} تجعل: {وتزكيهم بها} [منقطعا عن الأول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r13.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r13.claim: Alternatively the verb's subject is the addressee, as with the next verb; keeping the phrases connected is better when that reading is possible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p33/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل (التاء) في في {تطهرهم} ضمير المخاطب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r1.claim: The charity raises them from the hypocrites' station to the station of the sincere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r1.anchor: أي: ترفعهم بهذه الصدقة من منازل المنافقين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as accepting from them and turning toward them in repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r2.anchor: أشار ابن عباس في تفسير هذا الحرف فقال: أقبل منهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r3.claim: The command means to pray for them; prayer in Arabic means supplication.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r4.claim: The imam's practice after collecting charity should be to supplicate for the giver, asking God to reward the gift and bless what remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r4.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن السنة للإمام إذا أخذ الصدقة أن يدعو للمتصدق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r5.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r5.claim: When Abu Awfa brought his charity, the Prophet prayed, God, bless the family of Abu Awfa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r5.anchor: وقال رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r6.claim: A singular reading of the word prayer is also reported.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r7.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers the plural: he takes it for a small number, as in three, four, or five prayers, while the singular is more frequent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد (¬7): (الصلاة عندي أكثر من الصلوات؛ لأن الصلوات للجمع القليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r8.claim: Abu Hatim rejects the claim that a ta-marked plural indicates a small number, citing God's inexhaustible words in 31:27.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: (من زعم أن الجمع بالتاء تقليل فقد غلط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r9.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r9.claim: Prayer as a verbal noun can have singular form while denoting a collective, as in 8:35 and 31:19; named, frequently used verbal nouns can also pluralize, and distinct kinds make pluralization apt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r9.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي: (الصلاة مصدر يقع على الجميع والمفرد بلفظ واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r10.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r10.claim: Some prefer the plural because the Quran's written form has a waw here, in Hud, and in al-Mu'minun, while the form in al-Sa'ila is written without one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: (الصلوات) في هذه السورة وفي هود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r11.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r11.claim: Some reject the claim that singular is better because it denotes abundance and plural denotes few: ta-marked plurals can denote many, as in 34:37 and 33:35.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p35/r11.anchor: قال: (ومن زعم أن (الصلاة) أولى لأن (الصلاة) للكثرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r1.claim: Sakan is what one finds rest in; the Prophet's prayers are something their souls can rest in.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r1.anchor: السكن في اللغة: ما سكنت إليه، فالمعنى: إن دعواتك مما تسكن إليه نفوسهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r2.claim: The Prophet's supplication is mercy for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: دعاؤك رحمة لهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r3.claim: The prayer gives them dignity and composure.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r4.claim: It reassures them that God has accepted their charity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (طمأنينة لهم أن الله قد قبل منهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r5.speaker: الكفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r5.claim: The Prophet's seeking forgiveness calms their hearts and assures them God has accepted their repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r5.anchor: وقال الكفراء: (استغفر لهم؛ فإن استغفارك لهم تسكن إليه قلوبهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p38/r6.claim: God hears what they say and knows their regret and return to Him.

QASHANI:9:103/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r1.claim: The companions first received the Prophet's spiritual training and purification; then charity is prescribed because wealth manifests ego, strengthens its traits, and feeds its desires.
QASHANI:9:103/r1.anchor: ولما وفقوا للقسم الأول ببركة صحبة الرسول وتزكيته إياهم وتربيته لهم قال:

QASHANI:9:103/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r2.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
QASHANI:9:103/r2.claim: The Prophet calls wealth a source or fuel of desires.
QASHANI:9:103/r2.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام: " المال مادة الشهوات "

QASHANI:9:103/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r3.claim: Their first spiritual state should be detachment from wealth, weakening egoic powers and desires and purifying dark dispositions, sins, and satanic impulses.
QASHANI:9:103/r3.anchor: فينبغي أن يكون أول حالهم التجرد عن الأموال لتنكسر قوى النفس وتضعف أهواؤها وصفاتها

QASHANI:9:103/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r4.claim: Praying for them means directing spiritual aspiration and pouring out the light of companionship upon them.
QASHANI:9:103/r4.anchor: بإمداد الهمة وإفاضة نور الصحبة عليهم

QASHANI:9:103/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r5.claim: The Prophet's attention, spiritual force, and blessed companionship bring tranquility down into their hearts and make them secure.
QASHANI:9:103/r5.anchor: إن نورك الذي تفيض عليهم بالتفات خاطرك إليهم وقوة همتك وبركة صحبتك سبب نزول السكينة فيهم

QASHANI:9:103/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r6.claim: Sakīna is a settled light in the heart that steadies its orientation to God, strengthens certainty, and frees it from satanic and egoic agitation.
QASHANI:9:103/r6.anchor: والسكينة نور مستقر في القلب يثبت معه في التوجه إلى الحق ويتقوى اليقين

QASHANI:9:103/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:9:103/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:9:103/r7.claim: God hears their supplication and confession of sins and knows their intentions, resolve, remorse, and inward grief.
QASHANI:9:103/r7.anchor: يسمع تضرعهم واعترافهم بذنوبهم { عليم } يعلم نياتهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r1.claim: The Messenger took a third of their wealth, and the charity expiated their sins.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r1.anchor: فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلث أموالهم، وكانت كفارة للذنوب التي أصابوها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r2.claim: The charity purifies them from sins.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r3.claim: Through the charity, Muhammad raises them from the ranks of hypocrites.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r3.anchor: ترفعهم أنت يا محمد بهذه الصدقة من منازل المنافقين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r4.claim: The command is to supplicate for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r4.anchor: ادع لهم { إن صلاتك سكن لهم } إن دعواتك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r5.claim: The Prophet's supplications reassure them that God accepted their repentance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r5.anchor: إن دعواتك مما تسكن نفوسهم إليه بأن قد تاب الله عليهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:103-104/r6.claim: God hears what they say and knows their remorse.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r8.claim: Once released, they offered their property for alms and purification; the Prophet said he had not been ordered to take anything from them, after which this verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r8.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm da “emvâlinizden bir şey almakla emrolunmadım” buyurdu. Ba‘dehu şu âyet nâzil oldu:

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r9.claim: The alms cleanse them of the stains of sin and increase their good deeds, raising them to the rank of the sincere.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r9.anchor: günah lekelerinden temizlenmelerine ve hasenâtlarının tenmiyesiyle muhlisler derecesine terfî‘lerine sebep olasın.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r10.claim: Taking مِن as partitive, Elmalılı reports that the Prophet took one third of their property, not all of it.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r10.anchor: mallarının hepsini değil مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ kaydındaki teb‘îza mürâ‘ât ederek üçte birini ahz eyledi denilmiştir.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r11.speaker: Hasen-i Basrî
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r11.claim: Hasan al-Basri says this is a special, voluntary expiation for sins, not obligatory zakat or a financial penalty; it depends on willingness and intention.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r11.anchor: Hasen-i Basrî’nin kavli budur. Ma‘amâfîh bir cezâ-yı mâlî mâhiyetinde değil, tav‘u niyete mütevakkıf bir sadaka olmak üzeredir.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r12.speaker: ekser-i fukahâ
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r12.claim: Most jurists take the command to concern obligatory zakat: the passage addresses the wealthy, love of wealth caused the sin, and willingly paying their due zakat would demonstrate sincere repentance and remove hypocrisy.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r12.anchor: Fakat ekser-i fukahâ demişlerdir ki bundan asıl murad farz olan zekâttır.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r13.claim: Elmalılı favors the obligatory-zakat reading while allowing extra voluntary gifts; on the alternative reading, the command requires the Prophet to take and accept expiatory alms, and thus more clearly applies to obligatory zakat.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r13.anchor: farz olan zekâtların ahz ve kabûlüne evleviyetle delâlet edeceği derkârdır.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r14.claim: The Prophet's statement that he was not ordered to take their property may concern the refusal to accept alms from some, such as Hatib ibn Saʿlaba.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r14.anchor: “emrolunmadım” buyurmasının da Hâtıb b. Sa‘lebe gibi [2613] birtakımlarının sadakalarının kabûlünden memnû‘iyet meselesiyle alâkası muhtemildir.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r15.claim: The Prophet could not take charity for himself: obligatory alms were forbidden to the Prophet's family, and both obligatory and voluntary charity were forbidden to him.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r15.anchor: Âl-i Resûl fukarâsının sadakāt-ı vâcibeyi kabul etmeleri haram olduğu gibi Resûlullah’a vâcib ve tetavvu‘her sadaka haram idi.

ELMALILI:9:101-106/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r16.claim: The Prophet's collection under the cited hadith was in his capacity as imam, who must collect and distribute alms; the verse establishes this duty and connects to the collectors of 9:60.
ELMALILI:9:101-106/r16.anchor: bu âyet her hâlde sadakātın ahzında imamın bir vazifesi bulunduğuna delâlet eder ki وَٱلْعَٰمِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا [et-Tevbe 9/60] bununla alâkadardır.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r1.claim: The quoted legal discussion says collecting alms belongs to the imam; a payer's direct payment to the poor does not suffice because the imam's right to collect remains.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r1.anchor: Bu âyet delâlet eder ki sadakātı ahz, imama aittir.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r2.claim: The Prophet sent collectors for livestock and ordered them to take alms at the animals' locations and watering places.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem mevâşî sadakātına âmiller gönderir ve onlara mevâşînin mevzilerinde, sular üzerinde sadakalarının ahzını emrederdi

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r3.claim: The Prophet's condition to the Thaqif delegation that they would not be assembled or tithed meant they need not bring livestock to collectors; collectors would visit watering and likely grazing places to collect.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r3.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’ın Sakif vefdine بأن لا يحشروا ولا يعشروا diye şart etmesinin de mânası budur.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r4.claim: The same collection procedure applies to zakat on crops and fruit.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r4.anchor: Kezâlik sadakāt-ı simâr (hububat ve meyve) de böyle olacaktır.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r5.claim: Zakat on hidden assets was brought to the Prophet and the first caliphs, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r5.anchor: Diğer zekât-ı emvâl -yani emvâl-i bâtıne- ise Resûlullah’a ve Ebû Bekir’e ve Ömer’e ve Osman’a götürülürdü.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r6.speaker: عثمان
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r6.claim: Uthman announced in Ramadan that debt should be paid first and the remaining wealth purified with zakat; he then left payment to the poor to each person's choice, ending the imam's collection right through a binding act of a just imam.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r6.anchor: ‘Bu ay zekâtlarınız ayıdır. Her kimin üzerinde deyni varsa te’diye etsin, sonra da bakıyye-i malını tezkiye eylesin’ dedi ve binâen‘aleyh mesâkîne edâsını [2614] herkesin kendisine bıraktı

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r7.claim: Uthman's policy was a valid agreement made by a just imam, binding on the community and therefore ending the imam's collection right in that case.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r7.anchor: Çünkü bu, eimme-i adlden bir imamın akdeylediği bir akiddir. Ve binâen‘aleyh ümmet üzerine nâfizdir.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r8.claim: Collectors were not sent for hidden wealth because it was concealed in protected homes and shops, agents could not enter them, and owners could not be compelled to produce all their assets; owners brought this zakat and their declarations were accepted.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r8.anchor: öyle emvâl-i bâtıne zekâtlarına sâ‘î gönderilmemiş idi, imama kendileri getirirler ve bu babda kavilleri makbul olurdu.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r9.claim: When hidden assets circulated between towns as trade and became visible, collectors were appointed to take their zakat, as with livestock.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r9.anchor: bu emvâl, beldeden beldeye sevk ile tasarruf olunup mevâşî gibi zâhire çıktığı zaman bunlarda vâcib olan zekâtı ahzetmek için de âmiller nasbolunmuştur.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r10.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r10.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz instructed collectors to take half a dinar per twenty from Muslim trade goods and one dinar per twenty from dhimmi goods, only after a year, citing a report traced to someone who heard the rule from the Prophet.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r10.anchor: Nitekim Ömer b. Abdülaziz müslimin[^15] mürur ettirdiği ticârâttan her yirmi dinarda yarım dinar, zimmînin geçirdiğinden her yirmi dinarda bir dinar alınmasını

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r11.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r11.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab had earlier instructed collectors to take a quarter-tithe from Muslims, a half-tithe from dhimmis, and a full tithe from those at war with the Muslims.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r11.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer b. el-Hattab âmillerine müslimden rub‘-i öşür, zimmîden nısf-ı öşür, harbîden öşür almalarını yazmış idi

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r12.claim: For Muslims, collection is obligatory zakat and requires the conditions of a completed year, nisab, and valid ownership; if zakat is not due, nothing is taken.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r12.anchor: müslimden alınan zekât-ı vâcibe olup bunda havl ve nisâb[^16] ve sıhhat-i milk gibi şerâit-i vücub muteber olur, eğer zekât vâcib değilse alınmazdı.

ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r13.claim: Umar's practice followed the Prophet's collection of livestock, fruits, and crops; because trade goods circulated openly in Muslim lands and no Companion objected, the rule became consensus, which Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz also followed with the cited hadith.
ELMALILI:9:101-106#2/r13.anchor: Ashabdan bir kimse de buna itiraz ve muhalefet etmemiş binâen‘aleyh bir icmâ‘olmuştu. Ve işte Ömer b. Abdülaziz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r1.claim: After regretting their absence from Tabuk, some people brought their property for purification and distribution and asked the Prophet to pray for forgiveness; he initially declined, and the verse then came down.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r2.speaker: âlimlerin bir kısmı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r2.claim: Some scholars, following the occasion report, understand the charity here as voluntary donations taken to expiate sins.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r2.anchor: buradaki sadaka ile, günahlara kefâret olmak üzere alınan gönüllü bağışların kastedildiği kanaatindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r3.speaker: bazı âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r3.claim: Other scholars reading the same report say the repentant people already owed zakat and asked the Prophet to accept the zakat they had previously withheld.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r3.anchor: zaten zekât ile yükümlüydüler; âyet Resûlullah’tan onların daha önce vermekten kaçındıkları zekâtı kabul etmesini istemiş oldu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r4.speaker: Fakihlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r4.claim: Most jurists treat the verse as the start of a new ruling that addresses collecting obligatory zakat.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r4.anchor: Fakihlerin çoğunluğuna göre ise âyet yeni bir sözün başlangıcıdır ve burada farz olan zekâtın alınması konusuna temas edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r5.claim: From early Mecca, the Qur'an linked belief in God's oneness with establishing socioeconomic balance and first built social awareness before setting detailed financial rules.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r5.anchor: Allah’ın birliği (tevhid) inancı ile sosyoekonomik dengenin kurulması ve korunması arasında çok sıkı bir bağ bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r6.claim: Eight Meccan verses use zakat, but not for the later fixed-threshold, fixed-rate Medinan levy; zakat was still a general duty whose amount Muslims set to their circumstances.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r6.anchor: Mekke döneminde inen sekiz âyette zekât kelimesi de kullanılmıştır; fakat bu âyetlerde geçen zekât kelimesiyle, Medine’de farz kılınan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r7.claim: After the Hijra, financial duties received fuller treatment: zakat appears as a definite noun in 22 more Medinan verses, while sadaqa, generally treated as synonymous, occurs in 12 Medinan verses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r7.anchor: bu dönemde yirmi iki âyette daha zekât kelimesi mârife (belirli isim) olarak kullanılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r8.claim: The fixed-threshold zakat was probably made obligatory in year two after the Ramadan fast, though this dating is uncertain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r8.anchor: nisabı ve miktarları belirli zekâtın –kesin olmamakla beraber– hicretin 2. yılında ramazan orucundan hemen sonra farz kılındığı anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r9.claim: The view that zakat became obligatory in year nine can be understood as dating the start of its regular state collection and distribution.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r9.anchor: zekâtın devlet tarafından düzenli bir şekilde toplanıp dağıtılmaya bu tarihte başlanmış olduğu şeklinde açıklamak mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r10.claim: Zakat literally includes increase, growth, purification, praise, and blessing; technically it is the prescribed share taken from qualifying wealth for Qur'anic recipients, and also the act of removing that share.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r10.anchor: Sözlükte “artma, çoğalma, arıtma, övgü ve bereket” gibi anlamlara gelen zekât, terim olarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r11.claim: The Qur'an's frequent pairing of zakat with prayer signals their strong connection; zakat is worship with moral and economic aims that benefits both the giver and society.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r11.anchor: Kur’an’da ve hadislerde hemen her zaman, bedenî bir ibadet olan namazla birlikte zikredilmesi bu iki dinî görev arasındaki güçlü bağı gösterir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r12.claim: Qur'an 9:60 lists zakat recipients, while Prophetic words and practice clarify eligible payers and assets, thresholds, amounts, timing, and payment method; jurists differ on some details.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r12.anchor: Zekâtın harcama yerleri Kur’an’da tek tek sayılmış olmakla beraber

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r13.claim: The prevailing view makes the Prophet the subject of both purification verbs; if the first verb instead describes charity, the verse means taking charity that purifies them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r13.anchor: arındırma ve temize çıkarma fiillerinin öznesinin Hz. Peygamber olduğu kanaati hâkimdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r14.claim: Tathir removes the harmful effects sins leave on people, while tazkiya means cleansing thoroughly and increasing blessing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r14.anchor: tathîr, “günahların onların üzerinde bıraktığı kötü etkileri gidermek”, ikincisinin masdarı olan tezkiye ise

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r15.claim: The Prophet's prayer for them means praying for them and asking forgiveness for their sins.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r15.anchor: “senin onlar için duada bulunman, günahlarının bağışlanmasını istemen” anlamıyla

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r16.claim: His prayer is explained as mercy that assures them their repentance is accepted, brings peace to their hearts, and honors them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:9:103/r16.anchor: “Onlar için rahmettir, tövbelerinin kabul edildiği inancını sağlar ve gönüllerini huzura kavuşturur, onları şereflendirir”

BURHAN:v3p94/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.claim: An inna-clause may provide the reason for the preceding command or statement, as in seeking forgiveness, praying for people, and disclaiming a blameless self.
BURHAN:v3p94/r5.anchor: وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم

BURHAN:v3p91/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r1.claim: Explicitly stating a cause is more emphatic than giving a ruling without its cause: the named cause supports generalizing the effect, and people are more inclined to transmit rulings whose rationale is stated.
BURHAN:v3p91/r1.anchor: بأن يذكر الشيء معللا فإنه أبلغ من ذكره بلا علة لوجهين أحدهما أن العلة المنصوصة قاضية بعموم المعلول

BURHAN:v3p91/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r2.claim: Most Qurʾanic causal clauses answer an unstated ‘why?’ prompted by the preceding statement; the causal sense is evident because a causal فاء could replace إن here.
BURHAN:v3p91/r2.anchor: وغالب التعليل في القرآن فهو على تقدير جواب سؤال اقتضته الجملة الأولى وهو سؤال عن العلة

BURHAN:v2p165/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r7.claim: When two equally clear literal meanings differ as linguistic and legal senses, the legal sense takes priority unless context indicates the linguistic one; customary usage outranks linguistic, while legal usage outranks customary.
BURHAN:v2p165/r7.anchor: فالشرعية أولى إلا أن تدل قرينته على إرادة اللغوية نحو قوله تعالى ﴿ وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p405/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p405/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p405/r6.claim: In وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم, إن explains the command and answers the implied question about why the Prophet should pray for them.
BURHAN:v2p405/r6.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى ﴿ وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم ﴾ واعلم ان كل جملة صدرت بان مفيدة للتعليل

BURHAN:v2p405/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p405/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p405/r7.claim: A causal clause introduced by إن that also answers an implied question can instead use ف to preserve the cause while dropping the question-answer force.
BURHAN:v2p405/r7.anchor: فان الفاء يصح ان تقوم فيها مقام ان مفيدة للتعليل حسن تجريدها عن كونها جوابا للسؤال

BURHAN:v4p105/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p105/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p105/r1.claim: The statement that the Prophet's prayer is comfort for them explains the preceding command to pray for them.
BURHAN:v4p105/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ إن صلاتك سكن لهم ﴾ 11 فانها بيان للامر بالصلاة

SULAMI:v1p284#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r1.claim: Some say taking their charity purifies them through zakat and from the stain of created things, while the Prophet's prayers settle them toward the afterlife and cut them off from worldly attachment.
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : خذ منهم الصدقة فإن أخذك يطهرهم لإعطاء الزكاة

SULAMI:v1p284#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r2.speaker: رويم
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r2.claim: Ruwaym reads purification and growth as cleansing their inner secrets and refining their souls.
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r2.anchor: قال رويم : تطهر سرائرهم وتزكي نفوسهم

SULAMI:v1p284#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r3.claim: One gloss takes the command to pray over them as a command to supplicate for them; the Prophet's prayer turns them toward the afterlife and away from the world.
SULAMI:v1p284#3/r3.anchor: وقيل في قوله عز وجل : ﴿ وصل عليهم ﴾ : أي : ادع لهم

ITQAN:v2p454#4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p454#4/r2.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v2p454#4/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni and rhetoricians allow inna to mean “because”; in the cited command to pray for them, it introduces the reason their prayer is a comfort, a kind of emphasis.
ITQAN:v2p454#4/r2.anchor: والثاني التعليل أثبته ابن جني وأهل البيان

ITQAN:v4p480/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p480/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p480/r4.claim: What scholars determine by ijtihad includes deriving rulings, explaining what is general or ambiguous, and specifying general wording.
ITQAN:v4p480/r4.anchor: وأما ما يعلمه العلماء ويرجع إلى اجتهادهم فهو الذي يغلب عليه إطلاق التأويل وذلك استنباط الأحكام وبيان المجمل وتخصيص العموم

ITQAN:v4p480/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p480/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p480/r5.claim: When a word has several meanings, only scholars should use evidence rather than mere opinion; choose the clearer meaning unless proof points to a less obvious one.
ITQAN:v4p480/r5.anchor: وكل لفظ احتمل معنيين فصاعدا فهو الذي لا يجوز لغير العلماء الاجتهاد فيه وعليهم اعتماد الشواهد والدلائل دون مجرد الرأي

ITQAN:v4p480/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p480/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p480/r6.claim: If equally plausible literal meanings differ between ordinary language and the legal convention, prefer the legal meaning unless context indicates the linguistic one, as with the Prophet’s prayer for alms givers.
