ITQAN:v4p480/r6.anchor: فالحمل على الشرعية أولى إلا أن يدل دليل على إرادة اللغوية

ITQAN:v2p313#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p313#2/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p313#2/r11.claim: Sakan means mercy or reassurance for them.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r1.claim: The emphatic clause after the commands in 9:103 confirms their significance; the author lists this alongside other Qurʾānic instances, including Luqmān’s counsel.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r1.anchor: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r2.claim: The pronoun of the affair has a special delicacy when followed by إن; with conditional constructions it is scarcely found without إن, which makes the clause fit the pronoun.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r2.anchor: ومن خصائصها أنك ترى لضمير الأمر والشأن معها من الحسن واللطف ما لا تراه إذا هي لم تدخل عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan allows إنّها لا تعمى الأبصار to refer forward to الأبصار, with the pronoun placed before its explanation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r3.anchor: وأجاز أبو الحسن فيها وجها آخر ، وهو أن يكون الضمير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r4.claim: Even on Abū al-Ḥasan’s parse, إن remains necessary; the author rejects هي لا تعمى الأبصار as an ungrammatical alternative.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r4.anchor: والحاجة في هذا الوجه أيضا إلى ' إن ' قائمة كما كانت في الوجه الأول

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r5.claim: Although قل هو الله أحد begins with an ungoverned pronoun of the affair, such a pronoun is rarely used with a conditional clause; some also allow a non-affair reading there.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p243/r5.anchor: على أنهم قد أجازوا في ( ﴿ قل هو الله أحد ﴾ ) أن لا يكون الضمير للأمر

AKHFASH:v1p364/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p364/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p364/r3.claim: Wa-tuzakkīhim bihā may start an independent clause, or describe ṣadaqa and then be repeated as emphasis; the same analysis is allowed for tuṭahhiruhum.
AKHFASH:v1p364/r3.anchor: فقوله {وتزكيهم بها} على الابتداء وان شئت جعلته من صفة الصدقة

DAMGHANI:v1p242/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r1.claim: Sakan and sakīna mean tranquility or reassurance for the heart.
DAMGHANI:v1p242/r1.anchor: السكن والسكينة بمعنى الطمأنينة قوله تعالى في سورة براءة

DAMGHANI:v1p282/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r11.claim: The Prophet’s ṣalāt for the alms-givers means asking forgiveness for them, which comforts them.
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r11.anchor: الصلاة الاستغفار قوله تعالى في سورة براءة وصل عليهم ان صلاتك سكن لهم اي استغفر لهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r2.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s cited verse supports the lexical sense of ṣalāt as supplication.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r2.anchor: الصلاة في اللغة : الدعاء . وأنشدوا من ذلك للأعشى :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r3.claim: Some derive the ritual prayer’s name from the supplication it contains.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن الصلاة الشرعية إنما سميت صلاة لما فيها من الدعاء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r4.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r4.claim: Others derive its name from the bowing and prostration that raise the ṣalā.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون سميت صلاة لما فيها من الركوع والسجود الذي [ يكون ]

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r5.claim: Ibn Fāris identifies ṣalā as the place where a horse’s tail is set.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r5.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والصلا مغرز الذنب من الفرس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r6.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r6.claim: Ibn Fāris also relates prayer to softening wood, since the worshipper becomes gentle and humble.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r6.anchor: قال : ويقال إنها من : صليت العود إذا لينته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r10.claim: Ṣalāt in the command to pray over the almsgivers means supplication.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r10.anchor: والرابع : الدعاء . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r1.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r1.claim: Thaʿlab defines ṭahūr as pure in itself and purifying of something else; clean clothing is free of dirt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r1.anchor: قال ثعلب : الطهور : الطاهر في نفسه المطهر لغيره . ويقال : فلان طاهر الثياب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r8.claim: Ṭahāra can mean purification from sins; alms purify and cleanse their givers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p419/r8.anchor: والسابع : الطهارة من الذنوب . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

FARRA:v1p450/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p450/r6.claim: The penitents had tied themselves to mosque pillars and vowed to stay until forgiven; after repentance came, they offered their wealth, but the Prophet waited for revelation before taking it, and then took some.
FARRA:v1p450/r6.anchor: وكان هؤلاء قد أوثقوا أنفسهم بسواري المسجد، وحلفوا ألا يفارقوا ذلك حتى تنزل توبتهم،

FARRA:v1p450/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p450/r7.claim: صل عليهم means seek forgiveness for them; the Prophet's intercession settles their hearts and reassures them that God accepted their repentance.
FARRA:v1p450/r7.anchor: وصل عليهم: استغفر لهم فإن استغفارك لهم تسكن إليه قلوبهم،

FARRA:v1p450/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p450/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p450/r8.claim: A plural reading صلواتك is reported, though the singular الصلاة is more frequent.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r1.claim: Here الصلاة means supplication: pray for them, since the Prophet's prayer calms them and reassures their hearts.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r1.anchor: ادع لهم، إن ذلك مما يسكنهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r5.claim: The Prophet's prayer for the family of Abu Awfa asks God to show them mercy and forgive them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p255/r5.anchor: وقال النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اللهم صل على آل

MAJAZ:v1p268/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p268/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p268/r2.claim: The Prophet’s ṣalāh here means his supplication, a source of reassurance, calm, and hope for them. Al-Aʿshā’s verse asks for reciprocal prayer and protection.
MAJAZ:v1p268/r2.anchor: «إن صلاتك سكن لهم» (103) أي إن دعاءك تثبيت وسكون ورجاء، قال الأعشى

MAJAZ:v1p268/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p268/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p268/r3.claim: The reply in al-Aʿshā’s verse is read nominatively like “peace be upon you” in response to a greeting; some read it in the accusative as an imperative to repeat and pray with the same words.
MAJAZ:v1p268/r3.anchor: رفعته كرفع قولك: إذا قال السلام عليكم، قلت أنت: وعليك السلام وبعضهم ينصبه على الإغراء والأمر

NAHHAS:v2p233/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p233/r4.claim: The charity here is the obligatory zakah, according to the reports cited.

NAHHAS:v2p233/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p233/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers addressing the Prophet: you purify them and increase their purity through the charity.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الأجود أن تكون المخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي فإنك تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها

NAHHAS:v2p233/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p233/r6.claim: Another parsing takes the phrase as a circumstantial clause.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع الحال

NAHHAS:v2p233/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r7.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p233/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the pronoun to refer to the charity and treats بها as emphasis.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r7.anchor: قال الأخفش ويجوز أن تكون للصدقة ويكون ( بها ) توكيدا

NAHHAS:v2p233/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p233/r8.claim: A further parse attributes تطهرهم to the charity and تزكيهم to the Prophet.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تطهرهم للصدقة وتزكيهم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

NAHHAS:v2p233/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p233/r9.claim: A fifth analysis makes the verb jussive as the response to a command, with a poetic parallel quoted as evidence.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r9.anchor: والوجه الخامس أن تجزم على جواب الأمر كما قال ( قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب وعرفان )

NAHHAS:v2p233/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r10.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p233/r10.claim: One view says the command to pray for them was abrogated by the prohibition on praying over a dead hypocrite.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r10.anchor: أحدهما أنه منسوخ بقوله جل وعز ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا

NAHHAS:v2p233/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r11.speaker: العلماء
NAHHAS:v2p233/r11.claim: Scholars hold it was not abrogated: the Prophet prayed for contributors when they brought charity; his prayer reassured them and encouraged them to seek it.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r11.anchor: والآخر أنه غير منسوخ وأن المعنى وادع لهم إذا جاؤك بالصدقات وكذا كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يفعل والعلماء على هذا

NAHHAS:v2p233/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p233/r12.speaker: أهل اللغة
NAHHAS:v2p233/r12.claim: The linguists say ṣalāt in Arabic means supplication, as in the prayer over the dead.
NAHHAS:v2p233/r12.anchor: وحكى أهل اللغة جميعا فيما علمناه أن الصلاة في كلام العرب الدعاء ومنه الصلاة على الجنازة

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r1.claim: من أموالهم either attaches to خذ as a partitive preposition or modifies صدقة, originally as its adjective but advanced and made circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنه متعلق بـ " خذ " و " من " تبعيضية. والثاني: أن تتعلق بمحذوف لأنها حال من " صدقة "

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r2.claim: The tāʾ of تطهرهم can address the Prophet, making the clause circumstantial to the subject of خذ or an adjective of صدقة with an omitted بها; or it can be third-person with صدقة as subject, in which case it only modifies صدقة.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r2.anchor: يجوز أن تكون التاء في " تطهرهم " خطابا للنبي عليه السلام، وأن تكون للغيبة، والفاعل ضمير الصدقة

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r3.claim: In تزكيهم the tāʾ must address the Prophet, since بها refers to صدقة and the clause can be circumstantial or an adjective, with an omitted return pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r3.anchor: وأما " وتزكيهم " فالتاء فيه للخطاب لا غير لقوله " بها " فإن الضمير يعود على الصدقة

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r4.claim: Makkī allows تطهرهم to modify صدقة with a third-person tāʾ and تزكيهم to be circumstantial with an address tāʾ; the objection is that coordination normally requires the same syntactic role.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r4.anchor: وجوز مكي أن يكون " تطهرهم " صفة لصدقة على أن التاء للغيبة، و " تزكيهم " حالا من فاعل " خذ "

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r5.claim: Al-Samīn rejects Makkī's mixed parse under ordinary coordination, which would require both clauses to be adjectives or both circumstantial clauses; a circumstantial waw with an omitted-subject predicate for تزكيهم is possible but weak.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r5.anchor: فإن الواو مشركة لفظا ومعنى، فلو كانت " وتزكيهم " عطفا على " تطهرهم " للزم أن تكون صفة

SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r6.claim: Al-Samīn summarizes the available combinations: both clauses circumstantial with address, both adjectives with third-person and an omitted return, Makkī's mixed circumstantial option, or a weak predicate-of-an-omitted-subject parse for تزكيهم.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103/r6.anchor: فتلخص من ذلك أن الجملتين يجوز أن تكونا حالين من فاعل " خذ " على أن تكون التاء للخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads تطهرهم with a light form, deriving it from form IV أطهر, which takes an object through the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " تطهرهم " مخففا من " أطهر " عداه بالهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhawān and Ḥafṣ read singular صلاة in this verse and in 11:87; the other readers have plural صلوات in both. Here صلاة means supplication, while in 11:87 it means worship.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r2.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وحفص: " إن صلاتك " ، وفي هود: " أصلاتك تأمرك " بالتوحيد، والباقون:

SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r3.claim: Sakan means tranquility; an unnamed poetic line uses سكنا for a source of comfort, and al-Samīn concludes that here it means something calming for them, as indicated by لهم.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r3.anchor: والسكن: الطمأنينة قال: 2542 يا جارة الحي ألا كنت لي سكنا

SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ treats سكن as a passive-form noun, explaining why it is masculine; al-Samīn prefers an active sense, since that would mean a thing calming them, whereas the passive would require سكن إليها.
SAMIN-DURR:9:103#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولذلك لم يؤنثه " لكن الظاهر أنه هنا بمعنى فاعل

ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r1.claim: تطهرهم may modify صدقة as a purifying charity, though al-Zajjaj prefers construing it as addressed to the Prophet: you purify them with it.

ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r2.claim: تطهرهم may also be jussive as the response to the command: if you take their alms, you purify and cleanse them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r2.anchor: ويجوز " تطهرهم " بالجزم على جواب الأمر.

ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r3.claim: Recitation must retain the yāʾ in تزكيهم, following the written muṣḥaf.
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز في القراءة إلا بإثبات الياء في تزكيهم، اتباعا للمصحف.

ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r4.claim: صل عليهم means pray or supplicate for them, and سكن means they find repose through the prayer.
ZAJJAJ:v2p467/r4.anchor: أي ادع لهم. و (سكن) أي: يسكنون بها.

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r1.claim: Here sadaqah primarily means zakah, the obligatory purifying dues on Muslims whose property or income reaches a minimum.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r1.anchor: it primarily denotes the tax called zakah ("the purifying dues") incumbent on every Muslim enjoying a certain minimum of property and/or income

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r2.claim: A state's acceptance of zakah recognizes the giver as a Muslim in the Qur'anic sense.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r2.anchor: amounts to a recognition of the giver as a "Muslim" in the Qur'anic sense of this term

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r3.claim: The Prophet refused zakah from people whose conduct exposed them as hypocrites.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r3.anchor: the Prophet refused to accept it from all whose behaviour had made it obvious that they were hypocrites

ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r4.claim: The verse authorizes the Prophet and later Islamic authorities to accept zakah from people who demonstrate repentance through deeds.
ASAD-NOTES:9:102#n137/r4.anchor: to accept the payment of zakah from those who express their repentance by deeds as well as by

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r1.speaker: الكرماني
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r1.claim: Al-Karmani contrasts hypocrites, whose inward states only God knows (with the Prophet informed by Him), with believers, whose outward obedience is seen by God, the Messenger, and fellow believers.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r1.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني في هاتين الآيتين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r4.speaker: درة التنزيل
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r4.claim: The cited reading says the Prophet was commanded to have believers perform visible duties; unlike concealed hypocrisy, these deeds can be seen by God, the Messenger, and believers, which explains naming the latter witnesses.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#10/r4.anchor: وجاء في (درة التنزيل) أن الآية الثانية

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر، ونافع، وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r1.claim: These readers use the plural ṣalawātaka at 9:103 and also read the cited forms in Hud and al-Muʾminun as plurals.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر ونافع وابن عامر: إن صلواتك جماعة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r2.claim: Hafs reads the singular at 9:103 and Hud 11:87, but the plural at al-Muʾminun 23:9; that is the sole plural in this set.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: إن صلاتك على التوحيد، وفي سورة هود على التوحيد أيضا: أصلاتك فيهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the singular at all three locations; the cited other occurrences have no disagreement.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي في الثلاثة المواضع في سورة التوبة وهود والمؤمنين على التوحيد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r4.speaker: الأعشى
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r4.claim: Al-Aʿsha uses ṣallā for making a supplication, supporting Al-Farisi’s gloss that ‘pray for them’ means invoke for them so their hearts find calm and comfort.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: الصلاة في اللغة: الدعاء، قال الأعشى في الخمر :

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r5.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r5.claim: Sibawayh’s account does not take God’s ṣalāt on the Messenger as God supplicating for him; the idiom says the person merits such words, like ‘woe to the deniers.’
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r5.anchor: فأما قولهم: صلى الله على رسوله وعلى أهله وملائكته، فلا يقال فيه: إنه دعاء لهم من الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r6.claim: Ṣalāt, as a verbal noun, can have one form for singular and collective reference; its plural is also possible when its kinds differ, with Qurʾanic examples of both patterns.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p212/r6.anchor: وإذا كان الصلاة مصدرا وقع على الجميع والمفرد على لفظ واحد، كقوله: لصوت الحمير

NASHR:v2p281/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p281/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs read the phrase as singular with fatḥa on tāʾ; the others read a plural with kasra on tāʾ.
NASHR:v2p281/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص إن صلاتك على التوحيد وفتح التاء، وقرأ الباقون بالجمع وكسر التاء

QIRAAT-ER:9:103:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:9:103:13#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:9:103:13#1/r1.claim: The plural ṣalawāt reading presents the Prophet's prayers as multiple invocations or an ongoing supplicatory practice.
QIRAAT-ER:9:103:13#1/r1.anchor: Plural form (ṣalawāt) — canonical variant among 7 readers; pluralizes the Prophet's prayers, implying multiple invocations

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that, after being released, the confessors came with their wealth and asked the Prophet to give charity from it and seek forgiveness for them; he replied that he had not been commanded to take anything, and the verse was revealed. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r1.anchor: أخرج غير واحد عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم لما أطلقوا انطلقوا فجاءوا بأموالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r2.claim: Some narrations say the Prophet then took one third of their wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r2.anchor: فأخذ صلى الله عليه وسلم منها الثلث كما جاء في بعض الروايات

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r3.claim: Because obligatory zakat had already been prescribed, al-Alusi takes this charity as expiation for their sins, in keeping with its stated purifying effect.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r4.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r4.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the charity is zakat; taking it here prevents people from thinking these men were like certain hypocrites whose charity was rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r4.anchor: وعن الجبائي أن المراد بها الزكاة وأمر صلى الله عليه وسلم بأخذها هنا دفعا لتوهم إلحاقهم ببعض المنافقين

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r5.claim: On the expiation reading, 'their wealth' refers to these men who confessed; on the zakat reading, it may refer to owners of wealth generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r5.anchor: فضمير أموالهم لهؤلاء المعترفين وقيل : إنه على الثاني راجع لأرباب الأموال مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r6.claim: The plural 'wealth' indicates that the collection is taken from all categories of property.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r6.anchor: وجمع الأموال للإشارة إلى أن الأخذ من سائر أجناس المال

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r7.claim: The prepositional phrase may attach to 'take' or be an omitted circumstantial modifier of 'charity.'
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r7.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بخذ ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من ( صدقة )

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r8.claim: The ta in 'you purify them' addresses the Prophet; the jussive reading makes the clause a result of the command, while the nominative reading allows a circumstantial clause, an adjective for charity with an implied 'by it,' or an independent sentence, as Abu al-Baqa says.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r8.anchor: والتاء في ( تطهرهم ) للخطاب وقريء بالجزم على أنه جواب الأمر والرفع على أن الجملة حال

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r9.claim: On the adjective construction, the ta may instead be feminine third person referring to the charity, with no need to supply 'by it' because the following phrase indicates it.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r9.anchor: وجوز على إحتمال الوصفية أن تكون التاء للغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r10.claim: A reading has the form tutahhiruhum, from the causative verb athhara, meaning the same as tahhara, 'to purify.'
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r10.anchor: وقريء تطهرهم من أطهره بمعنى طهره

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r11.claim: With the yā retained, 'and you purify them' may predicate an omitted subject, serve as a circumstantial clause attached to the command or its response, or begin a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r11.anchor: بإثبات الياء وهو خبر مبتدأ محذوف والجملة حال من الضمير في الأمر أو في جوابه

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r12.claim: As a new sentence, it means the Prophet increases their good deeds or wealth through the charity, or intensifies their purification; interpreting it as raising them from hypocrites' ranks to sincere believers' ranks would imply they were hypocrites, contrary to the sounder view, and is tied here to the jussive reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r12.anchor: أي وأنت تزكيهم بها أي تنمي بتلك الصدقة حسناتهم وأموالهم أو تبالغ في تطهيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r13.claim: The apparent argument in al-Kashshaf makes the ta address the Prophet only, because the text says 'by it'; saying the charity itself purifies them is distant from Quranic eloquence.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r13.anchor: وظاهر مافي الكشاف يدل على أن التاء هنا للخطاب لا غير لقوله سبحانه : ( بها )

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r14.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r14.claim: Muslama ibn Muharib reads the verb without its yā: tazakkahum.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r14.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن محارب ( تزكهم ) بدون الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r15.claim: The command means pray and seek forgiveness for them; the preposition 'upon' is used because the verb carries a sense of kindness, and the ordinary supplication sense is more apparent than funeral prayer despite a report from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r15.anchor: أي ادع لهم واستغفر وعدى الفعل بعلى لما فيه من معنى العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r16.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r16.claim: Al-Shafi'i recommends the imam say to the giver: May God reward you for what you gave, make it purification for you, and bless what remains with you.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r16.anchor: واستحب الشافعي في صفته أن يقول للمتصدق آجرك الله فيما أعطيت

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r17.claim: Some require the imam's prayer for a donor; others require it for obligatory alms but recommend it for voluntary charity, or require it of the imam and recommend it of the poor recipient. Al-Alusi's preferred ruling is recommendation in every case.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r18.claim: Sakan is tranquility or what the soul rests in; one reading treats the Prophet's prayer itself as tranquility by hyperbole, another compares resorting to his prayer with resorting to a home, and al-Alusi prefers the first. His supplication soothes their hearts and assures them God has accepted them.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r18.anchor: والسكن السكون وما تسكن النفس إليه من الأهل والوطن مثلا وعلى الأول جعل الصلاة نفس السكن

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r19.speaker: غير واحد من السبعة
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r19.claim: Several of the seven canonical readers use the plural 'your prayers' to match the multiple people being prayed for.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r19.anchor: وقرأ غير واحد من السبعة ( صلواتك ) بالجمع مراعاة لتعدد المدعو لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r20.claim: God hears their confession, repentance, and supplication, and knows their regret, sorrow, and sincerity; alternatively He hears the Prophet's prayer and knows what wisdom requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r20.anchor: بما في الضمائر من الندم والغم لما فرط وبالا وبالإخلاص في التوبة والدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r21.claim: The closing names either reinforce the rationale for the prayer or form a concluding confirmation of the preceding two verses and all they contain.
ALUSI-FULL:v11p14/r21.anchor: والجملة حينئذ تذليل للتعليل مقرر لمضمونه وعلى الأول تذليل لما سبق من الآيتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.claim: The verse concerns people who stayed behind from the Tabūk expedition, repented, and bound themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet would release and excuse them; God revealed the verse and he released them. They offered their wealth for charity, but he said he had not been commanded to take it, and 9:103 then came down.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90/r5.anchor: فلما رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بهم فرآهم فقال: من هؤلاء؟ فقالوا: هؤلاء الذين تخلفوا عنك فعاهدوا الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in the report transmitted by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, says the penitents numbered ten, including Abū Lubāba.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r1.anchor: روي عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال: كانوا عشرة منهم أبو لبابة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭiyya counts five penitents, one of them Abū Lubāba.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r2.anchor: وروى عطية عنه: أنهم كانوا خمسة أحدهم أبو لبابة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وزيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam count eight penitents.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وزيد بن أسلم: كانوا ثمانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda count seven penitents.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r5.speaker: قالوا جميعا
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r5.claim: All these reports include Abū Lubāba among the penitents.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r6.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r6.claim: Some say the verse was revealed specifically about Abū Lubāba.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: نزلت في أبي لبابة خاصة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says Abū Lubāba's sin was telling Qurayẓa that surrendering to the Prophet's judgment meant death, while gesturing at his throat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: نزلت في أبي لبابة حين قال لقريظة: إن نزلتم على حكمه فهو الذبح وأشار إلى حلقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r8.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r8.claim: Al-Zuhrī says Abū Lubāba stayed behind from Tabūk, bound himself to a pillar, and abstained from food and drink for seven days until he collapsed; after repentance he waited for the Prophet to release him, then vowed to leave his home and give all his wealth, but the Prophet said one third sufficed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r8.anchor: وقال الزهري: نزلت في تخلفه عن غزوة تبوك فربط نفسه بسارية، وقال: والله لا أحل نفسي ولا أذوق طعاما ولا شرابا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r9.speaker: قالوا جميعا
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r9.claim: They say the Prophet took one third of the penitents' wealth and left two thirds, since God commanded taking some of their wealth rather than all of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r9.anchor: قالوا جميعا: فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلث أموالهم، وترك الثلثين، لأن الله تعالى قال: {خذ من أموالهم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say these penitents were distinct from the three who were left behind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p90#2/r10.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: هؤلاء سوى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r1.claim: The charity cleanses them of their sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r1.anchor: صدقة تطهرهم} بها من ذنوبهم، {وتزكيهم بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r2.claim: It raises them from the rank of hypocrites to that of the sincere; another explanation is that it increases their wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r2.anchor: ترفعهم من منازل المنافقين إلى منازل المخلصين. وقيل: تنمي أموالهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r3.claim: The command means to pray for them and seek forgiveness for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r3.anchor: {وصل عليهم} أي: ادع لهم واستغفر لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r4.claim: Another view gives the collector's prayer when receiving charity: May God reward you for what you gave and bless what you retained.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو قول الساعي [للمصدق] (2) إذا أخذ الصدقة منه: آجرك الله فيما أعطيت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r6.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read صلاتك in the singular; they also read the corresponding forms in Hūd 11:87 and al-Muʾminūn 23:9 singular.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r7.speaker: حفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ agrees with Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī on the singular reading here and in Hūd 11:87.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r7.anchor: وافقهما حفص ها هنا وفي سورة هود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r8.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r8.claim: The other readers use the plural in all three locations and pronounce the tāʾ here with kasra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91/r8.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالجمع فيهن ويكسرون التاء ها هنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains سكن as mercy for them through the Prophet's prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r1.anchor: {سكن لهم} أي: إن دعاءك رحمة لهم. قاله ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is reassurance and calm, giving them confidence that God accepted their repentance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: طمأنينة لهم، وسكون لهم، أن الله عز وجل قد قبل منهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses سكن as a strengthening of their hearts.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.claim: One legal view makes the imam's prayer obligatory when taking charity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في وجوب الدعاء على الإمام عند أخذ الصدقة: قال بعضهم: يجب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.claim: Another legal view considers the imam's prayer recommended when taking charity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم: يجب. وقال بعضهم: يستحب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r6.claim: A third view requires prayer for obligatory charity but recommends it for voluntary charity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يجب في صدقة الفرض ويستحب في صدقة التطوع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r7.claim: Another view requires the imam to pray and recommends that the poor recipient pray for the donor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: يجب على الإمام، ويستحب للفقير أن يدعو للمعطي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā reports that the Prophet prayed for people who brought charity, saying, O God, bless them; when Abū Awfā brought his charity, he prayed for Abū Awfā's family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r8.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن أبي أوفى -وكان من أصحاب الشجرة-قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r9.speaker: ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kaysān says this prayer concerns expiation for an oath, not obligatory charity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: ليس هذا في صدقة الفرض إنما هو في صدقة كفارة اليمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r10.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r10.claim: ʿIkrima says the reference is to obligatory charity; after the penitents' repentance, those who had not repented objected that they had been shunned the previous day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p91#2/r10.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هي صدقة الفرض، فلما نزلت توبة هؤلاء قال الذين لم يتوبوا من المتخلفين

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r1.claim: A report says that when released, they offered the wealth left behind and asked the Prophet to give it as charity and purify them; he replied he was not commanded to take their money, and the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r1.anchor: قالوا يا رسول الله هذه أموالنا التي خلفتنا فتصدق بها وطهرنا

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r2.claim: The charity purifies them from sins or attachment to wealth that could lead them to repeat the misconduct.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r2.anchor: من الذنوب أو حب المال المؤدي بهم إلى مثله

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r3.claim: One variant derives the verb from a form meaning “purify”; another makes it jussive as a response to the command.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r4.claim: Another reading makes the verb jussive as response to the imperative.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r5.claim: Through charity God increases their good deeds and raises them to the ranks of the sincere.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r5.anchor: وتنمي بها حسناتهم وترفعهم إلى منازل المخلصين

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r6.claim: Pray for them by showing care and asking forgiveness on their behalf.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r7.claim: The Prophet’s prayer settles their souls and reassures their hearts; its plural reflects multiple recipients.
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r7.anchor: تسكن إليها نفوسهم وتطمئن بها قلوبهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r8.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the word in the singular.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:103/r9.claim: God hears their confession and knows their remorse.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r9.claim: The command to take a portion of their wealth is a compassionate step after repentance and a pleasing offering that confirms acceptance.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r9.anchor: ولما كان من شأن الرضوان قبول القربان , أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم تطهيرا لهم وتطيبا لقلوبهم بقوله : { خذ } ورحمهم بالتبعيض

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r10.claim: The charity purifies them of sins and serves as expiation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r10.anchor: { تطهرهم } أي هي من ذنوبهم وتجري بهم مجرى الكفارة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r11.claim: He glosses the Prophet's role as increasing them through good deeds, with God hearing his supplication and knowing his reforming intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r11.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r12.claim: Here ṣalli means the Prophet's supplication and visible affection toward them; God hears his prayer and knows his sincerity.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r12.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r13.claim: The Prophet's prayer calms their hearts after anxiety about sin's outcome and reassures them that acceptance comes with God's approval.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r13.anchor: بعد قلق الخوف من عاقبة الذنب لما يعملون من أن القبول لا يكون إلا ممن حصل له الرضى عنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r14.claim: Their reassurance also rests on knowing that God hears the Prophet's supplication and knows his sincerity in seeking their reform.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r14.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r15.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r15.claim: Biqāʿī relates that the remorseful absentees tied themselves to mosque pillars; the Prophet waited for God's order to release them, then took one-third of their offered wealth as charity after this verse was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p381/r15.anchor: وذلك ان هذا الصنف لما اشتد ندمهم على التخلف اوثقوا أنفسهم بسواري المسجد فسأل عنهم رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that ten men delayed from Tabūk; seven tied themselves to mosque pillars until the Prophet released and pardoned them after God revealed 9:102. They offered their wealth for charity and forgiveness; after he said he was not commanded to take it, 9:103 directed him to take alms, purify them, and pray for them. Three others were deferred a year until the revelation of 9:117 and the passage about the three.
DURR-FULL:v4p274#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا} قال كانوا عشرة رهط تخلفوا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك فلما حضر رجوع رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the alms cleanse people of the sins they committed.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها} قال: من ذنوبهم التي أصابوا

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says praying for them means seeking forgiveness for their sins, and that the prayer is mercy for them.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وصل عليهم} قال: استغفر لهم من ذنوبهم التي أصابوها {إن صلاتك سكن لهم} قال: رحمة لهم

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says to pray for them means to supplicate for them; the Prophet's seeking forgiveness calms and reassures their hearts.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r3.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {وصل عليهم} يقول: ادع لهم {إن صلاتك سكن لهم} قال: استغفارك يسكن قلوبهم ويطمن لهم

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Awfā reports that the Prophet prayed for the family of whoever brought him alms; when Abū Awfā brought charity, he prayed for his family.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتى بصدقة قال: اللهم صل على آل فلان فأتاه أبي بصدقة فقال: اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفي

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses sakin as security for them.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {سكن لهم} قال: أمن لهم

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r6.claim: Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh reports that when his wife asked the Prophet to pray for her and her husband, he did so.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: أتانا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت له امرأتي: يا رسول الله صل علي وعلى زوجي فقال صلى الله عليك وعلى زوجك

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r7.speaker: يزيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r7.claim: Yazīd b. Thābit reports that the Prophet asked to be told when anyone died so he could pray over them, since his prayer over the deceased was mercy.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r7.anchor: عن خارجة بن زيد عن عمه يزيد بن ثابت - وكان أكبر من زيد - قال: خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v4p281/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r8.speaker: بشير بن الخصاصية
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r8.claim: Bashīr b. al-Khaṣāṣiyya advises that if alms collectors overcharge, people should gather their wealth and have the collectors pray for them, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v4p281/r8.anchor: عن دلسم السدوسي قال: قلنا لبشير بن الخصاصية: إن أصحاب الصدقة يعتدون علينا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after the confession verse was revealed, the Prophet released and excused the penitents; they brought their wealth and asked him to give it in charity and seek forgiveness for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت واخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم ارسل اليهم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فاطلقهم وعذرهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r2.claim: Ikrima says the commanded charity is taken from cattle, camels, sheep, and other kinds of wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : خذ من اموالهم صدقة قال : من البقر والابل والغنم وغيره

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r3.claim: Qatada says seven people stayed behind from Tabuk; four were those who mixed good deeds with bad, and they had vowed to fight and give charity.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : خذ من اموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها قال : ذكر لنا انهم سبعة رهط تخلفوا عن غزوة تبوك

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says these people had promised God that they would fight and give charity.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r4.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : خذ من اموالهم صدقة وكانوا وعدوا الله ان يجاهدوا ويتصدقوا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies them as hypocrites who had stayed behind at Tabuk, confessed hypocrisy and doubt, renewed their repentance, and offered their wealth to God; God then ordered the Prophet to accept charity to purify them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r5.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : خذ من اموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم ان صلاتك سكن لهم قال : هؤلاء

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says the charity cleanses them of the sins they committed.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1874#2/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك : فانزل الله عز وجل : خذ من اموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها من ذنوبهم التي اصابوا

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains their purification through charity as obedience to God and sincerity.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وتزكيهم بها يعني بالزكاة : طاعة الله والاخلاص

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains praying for them as seeking forgiveness for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r2.anchor: وبه عن ابن عباس وصل عليهم يقول : استغفر لهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r3.claim: Al-Suddi explains the command as praying for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r3.anchor: عن السدي قوله : وصل عليهم يقول : ادع لهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the Prophet's prayer as a source of comfort and delight for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : سكن لهم يقول : قرية لهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r5.claim: In another explanation, Ibn Abbas glosses their comfort as mercy.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : ان صلاتك سكن لهم يقول : رحمة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r6.claim: Qatada glosses their comfort as dignity and reassurance.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : ان صلاتك سكن لهم اي : وقار لهم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r7.claim: Qatada also glosses it as security for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1876/r7.anchor: عن قتادة : ان صلاتك سكن لهم قال : امن لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r1.claim: Because repentance requires repairing what can be repaired, this command follows the account of those who stayed behind: they missed both fighting and spending on the campaign, and their wealth can benefit Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r1.anchor: لما كان من شرط التوبة تدارك ما يمكن تداركه مما فات وكان التخلف عن الغزو مشتملا على أمرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r2.claim: The great expenditure on Tabuk depleted funds reserved for Muslim needs, so taking some wealth from those who stayed behind repairs part of the loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r2.anchor: استنفد المال المعد لنوائب المسلمين ، فإذا أخذ من المخلفين شيء من المال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r3.claim: A report says the repentant confessors offered the wealth that had caused them to stay behind and asked the Prophet to accept it, purify them, and seek forgiveness; he initially said he had not been ordered to take it, but accepted after this verse came down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r3.anchor: وقد روي أن الذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم قالوا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه أموالنا التي بسببها تخلفنا عنك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r4.claim: The pronoun in من أموالهم refers to another group of people who admitted their sins.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r4.anchor: فالضمير عائد على آخرين اعترفوا بذنوبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r5.claim: The tāʾ of تطهرهم can be second person, following the command خذ, or third-person feminine, referring to the charity; either reading shows that charity purifies and sanctifies.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r6.claim: Tazkiya is making something pure and abundant in good: purification removes sins, while sanctification adorns with virtues; cleansing precedes adornment, so the alms expiate sins and bring great reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى مقام التخلية عن السيئات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r7.claim: Praying for them means supplicating for them; the Prophet's prayer is supplication, whereas God's prayer is mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r7.anchor: الدعاء لهم . وتقدم آنفا عند قوله تعالى : { وصلوات الرسول } ( التوبة : 99 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abi Awfa says that after this verse the Prophet would say on receiving someone's alms, Allah, bless the family of so-and-so; his prayer joined the meaning of blessing with the word for prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p22/r8.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن أبي أوفى يجمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه في هذا الشأن بين معنى الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r1.claim: This clause explains the command to pray for them: the Prophet's supplication is a cause of calm, with سكن used metonymically for what produces tranquility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r1.anchor: سكن لهم ، أي سبب سكن لهم ، أي خير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r2.claim: Sakan is what one settles and rests in; figuratively, it is psychological calm, since fear unsettles the mind and causes anxiety. The Quran also uses it for night, homes, and a spouse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r2.anchor: أي يطمأن إليه ويرتاح به . وهو مشتق من السكون بالمعنى المجازي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r3.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet's prayer makes their souls more inclined to righteous acts: sin brings hesitation, while obedience brings assurance and certainty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r3.anchor: أو لأن دعاءه لهم يزيد نفوسهم صلاحا وسكونا إلى الصالحات لأن المعصية تردد واضطراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r4.claim: This closing statement suits the prayer command: hearing means answering supplication and hints that the Prophet's prayer is accepted; knowing hints that it brings great good and rectitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r4.anchor: ذكر العليم إيماء إلى أنه ما أمره بالدعاء لهم إلا لأن في دعائه لهم خيرا عظيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r5.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Asim through Abu Bakr, Abu Ja'far, and Yaqub read plural صلواتك; Hafs from Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read singular صلاتك. Both mean the Prophet's prayer generally: the definite plural explicitly includes its instances, while the singular implies them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p23/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.claim: Abū Lubāba and the repentant group offered their wealth as further repentance; the Prophet waited for revelation, then took a third of their wealth, which interpreters identify as the group intended here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r2.anchor: فروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ ثلث أموالهم مراعاة لقوله تعالى: من أموالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.speaker: جماعة من الفقهاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.claim: A group of jurists says the verse concerns obligatory zakat, addressed generally to people but specifically excluding non-zakat assets such as clothing and houses, and excluding slaves and similar categories.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r3.anchor: وقالت جماعة من الفقهاء: المراد بهذه الزكاة المفروضة، فقوله على هذا خذ من أموالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r4.claim: Because ṣadaqa is left general and needs specification, the verse implies that the imam collects alms and administers them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r4.anchor: وقوله صدقة مجمل يحتاج إلى تفسير، وهذا يقتضي أن الإمام يتولى أخذ الصدقات وينظر فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r5.claim: Min is partitive here; Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards this as the strongest grammatical interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r5.anchor: ومن في هذه الآية للتبعيض، هذا أقوى وجوهها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r6.claim: The best initial parse makes both verbs refer to the Prophet; alternatively they may be circumstantial of take or qualify ṣadaqa, with the latter strengthened by the verbs’ nominative form and بها meaning by the charity itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r6.anchor: وقوله تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها أحسن ما يحتمل أن تكون هذه الأفعال مسندة إلى ضمير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r7.claim: On the charity-as-subject parse, the donation itself purifies them of sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r7.anchor: ويكون قوله بها أي بنفسها أي يقع تطهيرهم من ذنوبهم بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r8.claim: Another possible parse makes تطهرهم an adjective of charity and تزكيهم a predicate of the Prophet or a circumstantial clause of charity, though the latter is weak because a circumstantial clause normally modifies a definite noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون تطهرهم صفة «للصدقة» ، وتزكيهم مسندا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r9.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r9.claim: Makkī also proposes that تطهرهم qualifies charity and تزكيهم is circumstantial of the pronoun in خذ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p77#2/r9.anchor: وحكى مكي أن يكون تطهرهم من صفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects Makkī’s parse because the conjunction wāw makes it amount to taking a purifying charity while the Prophet is himself purifying by it, an unsound meaning; without wāw it could work.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r1.anchor: وهذا مردود لمكان واو العطف لأن ذلك يتقدر خذ من أموالهم صدقة مطهرة ومزكيا بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r2.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan reads تطهرهم with a still ṭāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «تطهرهم» بسكون الطاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r3.claim: Ṣalli ʿalayhim means pray for them; the Prophet’s prayer brings calm, reassurance, and dignity to their souls as a sign of sound belief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r3.anchor: وقوله وصل عليهم معناه ادع لهم فإن في دعائك لهم سكونا لأنفسهم وطمأنينة ووقارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r4.speaker: مكي والنحاس وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r4.claim: Makkī, al-Naḥḥās, and others transmit a claim that this command was abrogated by the prohibition on praying over any hypocrite who dies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r4.anchor: وحكى مكي والنحاس وغيرهما أنه قيل إن هذه الآية منسوخة بقوله ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls abrogation a remote error: 9:84 concerns hypocrites treated as unbelievers, while this verse concerns repentant believers, so the commands do not conflict.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r5.anchor: وهذا وهم بعيد، وذلك أن تلك في المنافقين الذين لهم حكم الكافرين، وهذه في التائبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم ونافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ, and Ibn ʿĀmir read صلواتك in the plural, also in Hūd and al-Muʾminūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم ونافع وابن عامر «إن صلواتك» بالجمع، وكذلك في هود وفي المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read صلاتك in the singular; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī also use the singular in Hūd and al-Muʾminūn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r7.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «ان صلاتك» بالإفراد، وكذلك قرأ حمزة والكسائي في هود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r8.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r8.claim: ʿĀṣim alone reads the plural in al-Muʾminūn; readers agree in al-Anʿām and Sūrat Saʾala Sāʾil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في المؤمنين وحدها جمعا، ولم يختلفوا في سورة الأنعام وسأل سائل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r9.claim: The plural and singular readings both represent the verbal noun, expressed in one reading as singular and in another as plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r9.anchor: وهو مصدر أفردته فرقة وجمعته فرقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses sakan for them as mercy for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس سكن لهم رحمه لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r11.claim: Qatāda glosses sakan for them as dignity or gravitas for them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة سكن لهم أي وقار لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed and sought forgiveness for them when this verse was revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r12.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية فعل ما أمر به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r13.claim: The Prophet’s prayer comforts its recipient and strengthens hope, making the Prophet’s intercession a sound means of access to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r13.anchor: من يدعو له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنه تطيب نفسه ويقوى رجاؤه، ويروى أنه قد صحت وسيلته إلى الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r14.claim: God hears the prayer and knows whom to guide and pardon, along with what these attributes entail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p78/r14.anchor: سميع لدعائك عليم أي بمن يهدي ويتوب عليه وغير ذلك مما تقتضيه هاتان الصفتان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r1.claim: After God accepted the repentance of Abū Lubāba and his companions, they offered their wealth as charity; the Prophet replied he had not been ordered to take anything from them, and the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r1.anchor: لما تاب الله عز وجل على أبي لبابة وأصحابه قالوا يا رسول الله هذه أموالنا فتصدق بها عنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd and the majority identify this charity as a voluntary donation they offered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنها الصدقة التي بذلوها تطوعا قاله ابن زيد والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the charity as obligatory zakāt.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the final rāʾ in tuṭahhiruhum with sukūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن تطهرهم بها بجزم الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the phrase can modify ṣadaqa as an adjective, meaning a purifying charity; he considers the alternative construction better.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج يصلح أن يكون قوله تطهرهم نعتا للصدقة كأنه قال خذ من أموالهم صدقة مطهرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r6.claim: The better construction addresses the Prophet: taking their charity purifies them, with the jussive as the response to the command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r6.anchor: والأجود أن يكون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المعنى فانك تطهرهم بها ف تطهرهم بالجزم على جواب الأمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the charity purifies them of sins and makes them upright.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس تطهرهم من الذنوب وتزكيهم تصلحهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r8.claim: The yaʾ in tuzakkīhim must remain written, in conformity with the codex.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r8.anchor: ولا يجوز في تزكيهم إلا إثبات الياء اتباعا للمصحف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the command as asking forgiveness for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r9.anchor: أحدهما استغفر لهم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddī interprets it as praying for them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r11.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r11.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read ṣalawātika in the plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم إن صلواتك على الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r12.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read ṣalātika in the singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم إن صلاتك على التوحيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r13.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r13.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās explains the Prophet's prayer as reassurance that God has accepted their charity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r13.anchor: أحدها طمأنينة لهم أن الله قد قبل منهم قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses sakan as confirmation and calm.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r15.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa says it means mercy for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r15.anchor: والثاني رحمة لهم رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r16.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means nearness for them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r16.anchor: والثالث قربة لهم رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r17.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r17.claim: Qatāda explains it as dignity or respect for them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r18.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r18.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits the interpretation that it means purification for them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r19.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r19.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say the people in this account were other than the three who had been left behind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p495#2/r19.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة وهؤلاء سوى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r1.claim: God commands His Messenger to collect charity from their wealth to purify and cleanse them; Ibn Kathir says the command is general.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يأخذ من أموالهم صدقة يطهرهم ويزكيهم بها، وهذا عام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r2.claim: Some commentators restrict the pronoun to people who confessed their sins and mixed good deeds with bad; Ibn Kathir maintains the command's general scope.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r2.anchor: وإن أعاد بعضهم الضمير في "أموالهم" إلى الذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم وخلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r3.speaker: بعض مانعي الزكاة من أحياء العرب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r3.claim: Some Arab zakah refusers wrongly held that zakah must go to the Prophet alone, not the ruler; Abu Bakr and the Companions fought them until they paid it to the caliph, as before to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r3.anchor: ولهذا اعتقد بعض مانعي الزكاة من أحياء العرب أن دفع الزكاة إلى الإمام لا يكون، وإنما كان هذا خاصا برسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r4.claim: Abu Bakr swore that he would fight anyone withholding even an 'iqal—or, in another report, an 'anaq—that they used to give the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207/r4.anchor: حتى قال الصديق: والله لو منعوني عقالا -وفي رواية: عناقا -يؤدونه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأقاتلنهم على منعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.claim: Pray for them and ask forgiveness for them; Muslim reports that the Prophet prayed for the family of Abu Awfa when Abu Awfa brought his charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.anchor: أي: ادع لهم واستغفر لهم، كما رواه مسلم في صحيحه، عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتي بصدقة قوم صلى عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.claim: Another report says a woman asked the Prophet to pray for her and her husband, and he prayed for them both.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث الآخر: أن امرأة قالت: يا رسول الله، صل علي وعلى زوجي. فقال: "صلى الله عليك، وعلى زوجك"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.claim: Some reciters read the word in the plural, salawatuka; others read the singular, salatuka.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.anchor: قرأ بعضهم: "صلواتك" على الجمع، وآخرون قرءوا: {إن صلاتك} على الإفراد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sakin, the effect of the Prophet's prayer, as mercy for them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.claim: Qatada glosses sakin as dignity or solemn reassurance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: رحمة لهم. وقال قتادة: وقار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.claim: God hears the Prophet's supplication and knows who deserves it and who is worthy of it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r6.anchor: أي: لدعائك {عليم} أي: بمن يستحق ذلك منك ومن هو أهل له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Hudhayfa, and once directly to Hudhayfa, says the Prophet's prayer reaches a man, his child, and his grandchild.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p207#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن لحذيفة -قال مسعر: وقد ذكره مرة عن حذيفة -: إن صلاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لتدرك الرجل وولده وولد ولده

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim read ṣalātaka in the singular without wāw and with fatḥa on tāʾ, intending the collective sense; the same form appears in Hud.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: إن صلاتك بغير واو وفتح التاء على واحدة، والمراد به الجنس،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r2.claim: The other readers use the plural ṣalawātika, with wāw and kasra on tāʾ; the same plural is read in Hud.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون صلواتك بالواو وكسر التاء، وكذلك (هود) على الجمع فيها،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda prefers the singular because prayer is more frequent as a general practice; he argues that ṣalāt is used continually while ṣalawāt is a small plural, as in three or five prayers.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الأول أولى؛ لأن الصلاة أكثر، ألا ترى أنه قال: (أقيموا الصلوة) فكان على الأبد،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r4.claim: Abu Hatim rejects Abu Ubayda’s argument: the feminine plural suffix does not restrict a noun to a small number, as ‘God’s words are not exhausted’ shows.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: وهذا غلط؛ لأن الجمع بالتاء ليس للقليل، ألا ترى أنه تعالى قال: (ما نفدت كلمات الله)

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r5.claim: The source further objects that the plural here is not emphatic and notes that this reading is transmitted in the two sanctuaries and by most readers.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r5.anchor: والعجب من أبي عبيدة في قوله هذا والجمع لم يرد توكيدا، ألم يكن حاله دون الواحد، وبعد فإن تلك القراءة قراءة الحرمين،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r6.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r6.claim: The common reading has tuṭahhiruhum with ḍamma on rāʾ as a circumstantial clause, not a result clause.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r6.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: [تطهرهم] بضم الراء حالا لا جوابا،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r7.speaker: ابن محارب
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r7.claim: Ibn Muharib reads yuṭahhirhum and yuzakkīhim in the jussive as the result of the command.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن محارب: يطهرهم ويزكيهم بالجزم بالجواب،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reads yuṭahhiruhum with the lighter form IV verb aṭhara; the common reading is the form I ṭahara.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r8.anchor: عن الحسن يطهرهم بالتخفيف من أطهر يطهر، والقراءة الظاهرة من طهر يطهر.

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r11.claim: Amwāl is the plural of māl; tamawwala means acquiring wealth, and māla bi-māl means one’s wealth increased.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r11.anchor: والأموال: جمع مال، وتمول: اتخذ مالا، ومال بمال: إذا كثر ماله،

JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r12.claim: The plural ‘their wealth’ indicates different kinds of property, whereas the singular māl indicates one uniform kind.
JISHUMI:v5p3247#2/r12.anchor: وإنما ذكر بالجمع؛ لأن الأموال تدل على اختلاف الأجناس، فالأموال تقتضي الأجناس المختلفة، والمال يقتضي الجنس المتفق.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r1.claim: After the repentance of Abū Lubāba and his companions, they offered property as charity; the Prophet waited for a command, and this verse came down.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما نزل في أبي لبابة وأصحابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the charity as a voluntary gift of property offered by them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r2.anchor: الصدقة التي بذلوها من أموالهم تطوعا , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r3.claim: ʿIkrima identifies it as obligatory zakat; the wording says “from their wealth” because zakat is due only on some kinds of property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r3.anchor: الزكاة التي أوجبها الله تعالى في أموالهم فرضا , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r4.claim: The charity purifies their sins and makes their deeds grow in goodness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as asking forgiveness for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r6.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses it as praying for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r7.claim: In a report through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses sakana as nearness to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r7.anchor: قربة لهم , قاله ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r8.claim: In a report through Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as mercy for them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r8.anchor: رحمة لهم , رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r9.claim: Qatāda glosses sakana as dignity and composure for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as reassurance for them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r11.claim: It can mean security for them, supported by a poet’s line saying a neighbor was a refuge when others were not.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r12.claim: One legal view obligates the collector to pray for the donor, based on the command’s apparent wording.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r12.anchor: يجب على الآخذ الدعاء للمعطي اعتبارا بظاهر الأمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r13.claim: Another view recommends but does not require the prayer: God, not the collector, rewards the charity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r13.anchor: لا يجب ولكن يستحب لأن جزاءها على الله تعالى لا على الآخذ

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r14.claim: A third view requires prayer for a voluntary contribution but only recommends it for obligatory zakat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r14.anchor: إن كانت تطوعا وجب على الآخذ الدعاء , وإن كانت فرضا استحب ولم يجب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r15.claim: A fourth view recommends prayer for a donor to the ruler but requires it for a poor recipient, who is not individually designated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r15.anchor: إن كان آخذها الوالي استحب له الدعاء ولم يجب عليه , وإن كان آخذها الفقير وجب عليه الدعاء له

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r16.claim: A fifth view requires prayer for a donor to the ruler, as this displays obedience deserving thanks, but recommends it for a poor recipient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r16.anchor: إن كان آخذها الوالي وجب , وإن كان الفقير استحب ولم يجب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r17.claim: A sixth view requires prayer if the donor asks for it and recommends it otherwise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r17.anchor: إن سأل الدافع الدعاء وجب , وإن لم يسأل استحب ولم يجب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r18.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
