MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r18.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā brought his people’s charity and asked the Prophet to pray for him; the Prophet prayed for the family of Abī Awfā.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p398#2/r18.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال : أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بصدقات قومي

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r5.claim: The three men later brought the wealth that had kept them from joining the campaign and asked the Prophet to give it in charity; he disliked taking it, so the command to take it was revealed.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r5.anchor: ثم جاءوا بأموالهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r6.claim: God commands the Prophet to take their alms to cleanse them of their staying behind and improve them through it.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r6.anchor: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم } من تخلفهم

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r7.claim: Praying for them means asking God to forgive them; the Prophet's prayer settles and reassures their hearts.
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r7.anchor: يعني إن استغفارك لهم سكن لقلوبهم

MUQATIL:9:102-103/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:102-103/r8.claim: God hears their request that the Prophet take their wealth as charity and knows what they said.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r1.claim: The alms expiate their sins; another reported view identifies them as zakat.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r2.claim: This clause describes the alms; its feminine ending may address the collector or refer to the feminine alms.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r2.anchor: وهو صفة لصدقة والتاءللخطاب أو لغيبة المؤنث

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r3.claim: In “purify them,” the second-person ending is necessarily direct address.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r3.anchor: والتاء فى ﴿ وتزكيهم ﴾ للخطاب لا محالة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r4.claim: Purification intensifies cleansing, or means growth and blessing in wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r4.anchor: والتزكية مبالغة فى التطهير وزيادة فيه أو بمعنى الانماء والبركة فى المال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r5.claim: Pray for and show mercy to alms-givers; the collector's sunnah is to pray for the giver when collecting.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r5.anchor: واعطف عليهم بالدعاء لهم وترحم والسنة أن يدعوا المصدق لصاحب الصدقة إذا أخذها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r6.claim: Kufans other than Abū Bakr read singular ṣalāt; an unnamed view says the plural better conveys the generic sense.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r6.anchor: صلاتك كوفى غير أبى بكر قيل الصلاة أكثر من الصلوات لانها للجنس

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r7.claim: The prayer reassures them that God accepted their repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r7.anchor: يسكنون إليه وتطمئن قلوبهم بأن الله قد تاب عليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r8.claim: God hears the Prophet's prayer or their confession and supplication, and knows their remorse and grief.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p108/r8.anchor: ﴿ عليم ﴾ بما فى ضمائرهم من الندم والغم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r3.claim: Qatada gives a similar account and says the charity command was revealed about these men.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r3.anchor: وقال بنحوه قتادة وقال: وفيهم نزل: «خذ من أموالهم صدقة» ذكره المهدوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r7.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r7.claim: Mujahid says the command was revealed specifically about Abu Lubaba after he signaled to Banu Qurayza that the Prophet would kill them if they submitted; remorseful, he bound himself to a mosque pillar and fasted until God forgave him, whereupon the Prophet ordered his release.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت الآية في أبي لبابة الأنصاري خاصة في شأنه مع بني قريظة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r8.speaker: الطبري عن مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r8.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Mujahid the account of Abu Lubaba’s repentance; Ibn Ishaq gives a fuller version in his biography.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r8.anchor: ذكره الطبري عن مجاهد، وذكره ابن إسحاق في السيرة أوعب من هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r10.claim: Malik transmits that the Prophet told Abu Lubaba that giving one-third would suffice when he asked about relinquishing his wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r10.anchor: وقال حين أصاب الذنب: يا رسول الله، أجاورك وأنخلع من مالي؟ فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.claim: The majority say the passage concerns Tabuk stay-behinds who bound themselves like Abu Lubaba, vowing not to free themselves until the Prophet released and forgave them; after the verse was revealed, he released them and they offered their wealth as charity for purification and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r11.anchor: والجمهور أن الآية نزلت في شأن المتخلفين عن غزوة تبوك، وكانوا ربطوا أنفسهم كما فعل أبو لبابة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r12.claim: The Prophet swore he would not release or excuse the stay-behinds until commanded, because they had turned away and stayed behind from the expedition.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103/r12.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " وأنا أقسم بالله لا أطلقهم ولا أعذرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r1.speaker: جويبر عن ابن عباس وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the charity as obligatory zakat; Juwair reports this from Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿIkrima holds it according to al-Qushayri.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r1.anchor: فقيل: هي صدقة الفرض قاله جويبر عن ابن عباس، وهو قول عكرمة فيما ذكر القشيري.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r2.claim: Another view restricts the command to those for whom it was revealed: the Prophet took one-third of their wealth, not obligatory zakat; Malik says one-third fulfills a vow to give all one’s property as charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو مخصوص بمن نزلت فيه فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ منهم ثلث أموالهم، وليس هذا من الزكاة المفروضة في شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r3.speaker: مانعو الزكاة على أبي بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r3.claim: Those who refused zakat to Abu Bakr argued that the command addressed only the Prophet, so zakat ended with his death; they claimed he alone gave them purification and prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r3.anchor: مانعو الزكاة على أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه وقالوا: إنه كان يعطينا عوضا منها

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r4.speaker: شاعر مانعي الزكاة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r4.claim: Their spokesman’s poem says they obeyed the Messenger while he lived, questions Abu Bakr’s rule, and threatens to withhold alms while they retain strength.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r4.anchor: ونظم في ذلك شاعرهم فقال: أطعنا رسول الله ما كان بيننا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr swore to fight anyone who separates prayer from zakat.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r5.anchor: وفي حقهم قال أبو بكر: والله لأقاتلن من فرق بين الصلاة والزكاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi calls the claim that the command applies only to the Prophet ignorant of the Qurʾan, the sources of law, and religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r6.anchor: ابن العربي: أما قولهم إن هذا خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا يلتحق به غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says Qurʾanic address takes different forms: universal to the community, exclusive to the Prophet in wording and meaning, or addressed to him in wording while shared by the community in meaning and practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#2/r7.anchor: ابن العربي: أما قولهم إن هذا خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi gives examples of address shared in practice by the community though directed to the Prophet: prayer at the sun’s decline, seeking refuge before reciting, and prayer in battle; he also cites commands to the Prophet about piety and divorce.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r1.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل قوله تعالى: { خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها }

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r2.speaker: بعض العرب وهم دوس
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r2.claim: Some Arabs of Daws use māl for clothing, goods, and merchandise, but not coined money.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r2.anchor: ذهب بعض العرب وهم دوس: إلى أن المال الثياب والمتاع والعروض. ولا تسمي العين مالا.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that on the Khaybar expedition they gained no gold or silver, only al-amwāl—clothes and goods—illustrating the Daws usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام خيبر فلم نغنم ذهبا ولا ورقا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r4.speaker: غيرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r4.claim: Others use māl for coined gold and silver.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r4.anchor: وذهب غيرهم إلى أن المال الصامت من الذهب والورق.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r5.claim: One view uses māl specifically for camels, as in the saying that wealth is camels.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r5.anchor: وقيل: الإبل خاصة ومنه قولهم: المال الإبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r6.claim: Another view applies māl to all livestock.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r7.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r7.claim: Thaʿlab says property below the zakat threshold in gold or silver is not called māl, citing a poem about never reaching the threshold.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r7.anchor: قال: ما قصر عن بلوغ ما تجب فيه الزكاة من الذهب والورق فليس بمال

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r8.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r8.claim: Abu ʿUmar says ordinary Arabic calls everything owned and possessed wealth; the Prophet’s saying about what a person truly retains supports this usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو عمر: والمعروف من كلام العرب أن كل ما تمول وتملك هو مال لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r9.speaker: أبو قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r9.claim: Abu Qatada says the Prophet gave him armor, which he exchanged for a garden; it was the first property he accumulated in Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r9.anchor: وقال أبو قتادة: فأعطاني الدرع فابتعت به مخرفا في بني سلمة فإنه لأول مال تأثلته في الإسلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r10.claim: An oath to give all one’s wealth as charity covers every kind of property, zakatable or not, unless the person intended a particular kind; another view limits it to zakatable property.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r10.anchor: فمن حلف بصدقة ماله كله فذلك على كل نوع من ماله، سواء كان مما تجب فيه الزكاة أو لم يكن

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r11.claim: The command is unrestricted as to what is collected, from whom, and how much; Sunnah and consensus specify details. Zakat is due on livestock, crops, gold, and silver, with disagreement over horses and other trade goods.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r11.anchor: قوله تعالى: { خذ من أموالهم صدقة } مطلق غير مقيد بشرط في المأخوذ والمأخوذ منه

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r12.claim: The commentary on horses and honey will come in the Bee sūra; crop zakat was treated under al-Anʿam, mines under al-Baqara, and jewelry in this sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r12.anchor: وسيأتي ذكر الخيل والعسل في «النحل» إن شاء الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r13.speaker: أبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r13.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Saʿid sets minimum thresholds of five wasqs of dates, five awaq of silver, and five camels.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#3/r13.anchor: روى الأئمة عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r1.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r1.claim: Scholars agree an uqiyya equals forty dirhams; a free Muslim holding 200 minted silver dirhams for a full year owes five dirhams, one-fortieth.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r1.anchor: وأجمع العلماء على أن الأوقية أربعون درهما فإذا ملك الحر المسلم مائتي درهم من فضة مضروبة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r2.claim: The reported rule requires a full year to pass over property before zakat is due; al-Tirmidhi transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r2.anchor: وإنما اشترط الحول لقوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r3.speaker: مالك والليث والشافعي وأكثر أصحاب أبي حنيفة وابن أبي ليلى والثوري والأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأبو ثور وإسحاق وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r3.claim: These jurists impose one-fortieth on all silver beyond 200 dirhams, however small or large the excess.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#4/r3.anchor: وما زاد على المائتي درهم من الورق فبحساب ذلك في كل شيء منه ربع عشره قل أو كثر

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والحسن وعطاء وطاوس والشعبي والزهري ومكحول وعمرو بن دينار وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r1.claim: This group says no zakat is due on silver above 200 dirhams until the excess reaches forty dirhams, then one dirham is due.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r1.anchor: وقالت طائفة: لا شيء فيما زاد على مائتي درهم حتى تبلغ الزيادة أربعين درهما

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r2.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r2.claim: The majority require zakat on gold at twenty dinars, valued at 200 dirhams, and above, relying on a report from ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r2.anchor: وأما زكاة الذهب فالجمهور من العلماء على أن الذهب إذا كان عشرين دينارا قيمتها مائتا درهم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r3.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says both transmissions of the report from Abu Ishaq through Damra and al-Harith from ʿAli are sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r3.anchor: قال الترمذي: سألت محمد بن إسماعيل عن هذا الحديث فقال كلاهما عندي صحيح عن أبي إسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r4.speaker: الباجي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r4.claim: Al-Baji says the report’s chain is weak, but scholarly agreement to apply it confirms the ruling’s soundness.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r4.anchor: وقال الباجي في المنتقي: وهذا الحديث ليس إسناده هناك، غير أن اتفاق العلماء على الأخذ به

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r5.speaker: الحسن والثوري وبعض أصحاب داود بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Thawri, and some followers of Dawud ibn ʿAli say gold is not zakatable until forty dinars.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r5.anchor: وروي عن الحسن والثوري، وإليه مال بعض أصحاب داود بن علي على أن الذهب لا زكاة فيه حتى يبلغ أربعين دينارا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r6.speaker: جماعة أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r6.claim: The author rejects the forty-dinar threshold on reports from ʿAli, Ibn ʿUmar, and ʿAʾisha that the Prophet took half a dinar per twenty and one per forty; all but the dissenters follow this.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r6.anchor: وهذا يرده حديث علي وحديث ابن عمر وعائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يأخذ من كل عشرين دينارا

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r7.speaker: الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r7.claim: The community agrees that fewer than five camels incur no zakat; at five, one sheep is due, including sheep or goats.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r7.anchor: الخامسة اتفقت الأمة على أن ما كان دون خمس ذود من الإبل

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r8.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r8.claim: Scholars agree that five camels incur one sheep as their prescribed payment.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r8.anchor: وهذا أيضا اتفاق من العلماء أنه ليس في خمس إلا شاة واحدة وهي فريضتها

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r9.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r9.claim: Livestock zakat schedules are laid out in Abu Bakr’s letter to Anas when he sent him to Bahrain.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r9.anchor: وصدقة المواشي مبينة في الكتاب الذي كتبه الصديق لأنس لما وجهه إلى البحرين

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r10.claim: For 121 camels, Malik gives the collector a choice of three bint labun or two hiqqas.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r10.anchor: فقال مالك: المصدق بالخيار إن شاء أخذ ثلاث بنات لبون، وإن شاء أخذ حقتين.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r11.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r11.claim: Ibn Shihab requires three bint labun at 121 camels until 130, when one hiqqa and two bint labun are due.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r11.anchor: وقال ابن شهاب: فيها ثلاث بنات لبون إلى أن تبلغ ثلاثين ومائة فتكون فيها حقة وابنتا لبون.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r12.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r12.claim: Ibn al-Qasim favors Ibn Shihab’s camel-zakat schedule.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r12.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: ورأيي على قول ابن شهاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r13.speaker: عبد العزيز بن أبي سلمة وعبد العزيز بن أبي حازم وابن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r13.claim: Ibn Habib says these jurists follow Malik’s ruling for 121 camels.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r13.anchor: وذكر ابن حبيب أن عبد العزيز بن أبي سلمة وعبد العزيز بن أبي حازم وابن دينار يقولون بقول مالك.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r14.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r14.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hay requires four sheep at 301, five at 401, then another sheep per hundred; the same is reported from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r14.anchor: قال: فيها أربع شياه، وإذا كانت أربعمائة شاة وشاة ففيها خمس شياه وهكذا كلما زادت

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r15.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r15.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi is reported to share al-Hasan ibn Salih’s sheep-zakat schedule.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r16.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r16.claim: The majority require three sheep at 201 sheep, none more until 400, then four; thereafter one additional sheep per hundred by agreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#5/r16.anchor: وقال الجمهور: في مائتي شاة وشاة ثلاث شياه، ثم لا شيء فيها إلى أربعمائة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r1.speaker: ابن عبد البر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr says Ibn al-Mundhir erred in this issue, misattributing views and confusing the matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r1.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: وهذه مسألة وهم فيها ابن المنذر، وحكى فيها عن العلماء الخطأ

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r2.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r2.claim: Abu ʿUmar says cattle-zakat reports in the canonical collections are mursal, interrupted, or stopped; mursal transmitters are more reliable than those connecting them through Tawus from Muʿadh.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r2.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وقد رواه قوم عن طاوس عن معاذ، إلا أن الذين أرسلوه أثبت من الذين أسندوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r3.speaker: بقية
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r3.claim: A connected version is transmitted by Baqiyya through al-Masʿudi, al-Hakam, and Tawus; the author notes disagreement about reports Baqiyya alone transmits from reliable narrators.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r3.anchor: وممن أسنده بقية عن المسعودي عن الحكم عن طاوس. وقد اختلفوا فيما ينفرد به بقية عن الثقات.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r4.speaker: الحسن بن عمارة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r4.claim: Al-Hasan ibn ʿUmara also transmits the report through al-Hakam, but scholars agree he is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r4.anchor: ورواه الحسن بن عمارة عن الحكم كما رواه بقية عن المسعودي عن الحكم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r5.claim: A sound connected report from Muʿadh says the Prophet sent him to Yemen and ordered one yearling or female yearling for thirty cows, one mature cow for forty, and one dinar or equivalent Maʿafir cloth from each adult.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال: بعثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى اليمن فأمره أن يأخذ من كل ثلاثين بقرة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r6.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhi authenticates the connected Muʿadh report on cattle and poll tax.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r6.anchor: ذكره الدارقطني وأبو عيسى الترمذي وصححه.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r7.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r7.claim: Abu ʿUmar says scholars agree on the Prophetic and Companion rule of one yearling at thirty cows and one mature cow at forty, except for a few who require one sheep per five cows up to thirty.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمر. ولا خلاف بين العلماء أن الزكاة في زكاة البقر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وأبو قلابة والزهري وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Qilaba, al-Zuhri, and Qatada require one sheep for every five cows until thirty.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r8.anchor: إلا شيء روي عن سعيد بن المسيب وأبي قلابة والزهري وقتادة فإنهم يوجبون في كل خمس من البقر شاة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r9.claim: The commentary summarizes zakat’s principles and details; livestock partnership rules will be treated in Sad.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r9.anchor: ويأتي ذكر الخلطة في سورة «ص» إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r10.claim: Ṣadaqa derives from truthfulness because it demonstrates sound faith and agreement between inward and outward belief, unlike those who disparage voluntary givers.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: { صدقة } مأخوذ من الصدق، إذ هي دليل على صحة إيمانه وصدق باطنه مع ظاهره

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r11.claim: The verbs may be circumstantial clauses describing the Prophet: take the charity while purifying and elevating them through it.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r11.anchor: حالين للمخاطب التقدير: خذها مطهرا لهم ومزكيا لهم بها.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r12.claim: Alternatively, both verbs may describe the charity itself; the addressee performs the purification, and biha returns to the indefinite noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعلهما صفتين للصدقة أي صدقة مطهرة لهم مزكية

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r13.speaker: النحاس ومكي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r13.claim: Al-Nahhas and Makki take tutahhiruhum as an adjective of the charity and tuzakkihim as a circumstantial clause from the Prophet in khudh.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r13.anchor: وحكى النحاس ومكي أن «تطهرهم» من صفة الصدقة «وتزكيهم بها» حال من الضمير في «خذ»

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r14.claim: Making the circumstantial clause refer to the charity is weak because a circumstantial clause ordinarily comes from a definite antecedent.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون حالا من الصدقة، وذلك ضعيف لأنها حال من نكرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r15.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers addressing the Prophet directly as a detached or resumed clause; the verbs may also be jussive in response to the command.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#6/r15.anchor: وقال الزجاج: والأجود أن تكون المخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي فإنك تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r1.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads tutahhiruhum with a silent ṭāʾ, deriving it through hamza from ṭahura/aṭhartuhu, like ẓahara/aẓhartuhu.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن تطهرهم بسكون الطاء وهو منقول بالهمزة من طهر وأطهرته

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r2.claim: The command establishes that every leader who collects charity should pray for the donor’s blessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r2.anchor: أصل في فعل كل إمام يأخذ الصدقة أن يدعو للمتصدق بالبركة.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r3.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet prayed for people bringing charity, and prayed specifically for the family of Ibn Abi Awfa when he brought his charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r3.anchor: روى مسلم عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى قال: " كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه قوم بصدقتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r4.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r4.claim: Some say the prayer is abrogated by the ban on praying over a dead hypocrite and restrict prayer to the Prophet alone, citing his special status, 24:63, and Ibn ʿAbbas’s reported prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r4.anchor: قالوا: فلا يجوز أن يصلى على أحد إلا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده خاصة لأنه خص بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to have said that prayers should be offered for no one except the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r5.anchor: وبأن عبدالله بن عباس كان يقول: لا يصلى على أحد إلا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r6.claim: The author prefers allowing prayers for donors: the address is not exclusive to the Prophet, and Muslims should follow his practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r6.anchor: والأول أصح فإن الخطاب ليس مقصورا عليه كما تقدم ويأتي في الآية بعد هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r7.claim: When donors bring their charity, the Prophet’s prayer settles their hearts and makes them glad.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r7.anchor: أي إذا دعوت لهم حين يأتون بصدقاتهم سكن ذلك قلوبهم وفرحوا به.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r8.claim: Jabir reports that his wife asked the Prophet to pray for her husband; he replied with a prayer for Jabir and his wife.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r8.anchor: روى جابر بن عبد الله قال: أتاني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت لامرأتي: لا تسألي رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r9.claim: Prayer here means mercy and supplication; al-Nahhas says Arab usage means supplication, as in funeral prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r9.anchor: والصلاة هنا الرحمة والترحم. قال النحاس: وحكى أهل اللغة جميعا فيما علمناه أن الصلاة في كلام العرب الدعاء

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r10.speaker: حفص وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r10.claim: Hafs, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the word in the singular; the other readers use the plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r10.anchor: وقرأ حفص وحمزة والكسائي «إن صلاتك» بالتوحيد. وجمع الباقون.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r11.speaker: القراء
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r11.claim: The same singular-versus-plural reading difference occurs in aṣalātuka taʾmuruka in Hud.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r12.speaker: قُرِئ
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r12.claim: A reading has sakan with a silent kāf.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r13.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r13.claim: Qatada glosses sakan as dignity and composure; it is what quiets souls and makes hearts tranquil.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:103#7/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: معناه وقار لهم. والسكن: ما تسكن به النفوس وتطمئن به القلوب.

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r1.claim: The wise should work through the rulings of sacred law and the manners of the spiritual path until wholly free of hypocrisy; admitting sin is a believer’s inheritance from Adam.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r1.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد بأحكام الشريعة وآداب الطريقة إلى أن يحصل الخلاص من النفاق

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r2.claim: A report says Adam wept over his sin for two hundred years until God accepted his repentance and forgave him; penitents should therefore weep and humble themselves often.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r2.anchor: روي أنه بكى على ذنبه مائتي سنة حتى قبل الله توبته وغفر ذنبه

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r3.claim: A penitent should send blessings on the Prophet, intercessor for prophets and saints; Adam sought God through Muhammad’s standing, and believers should ask forgiveness for all believing men and women.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r3.anchor: ويصلي على النبي عليه السلام فإنه شفيع لكل نبي وولي ولذا توسل به آدم

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r4.claim: Seeking forgiveness is the servant’s request that God pardon sins; God’s forgiveness means concealing them by grace rather than exposing or shaming the sinner.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r4.anchor: ومعنى الاستغفار سؤال العبد ربه أن يغفر له ذنوبه ومعنى مغفرته لذنوب عباده أن يسترها عليهم

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r5.claim: A condition of repentance is not to commit sin deliberately; what occurs through forgetfulness or error is pardoned by God’s grace.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r5.anchor: ومن شرط التوبة أن لا يتعمد ذنبا فإن وقع منه بسهو أو خطأ فهو معفو عنه

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r6.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r6.claim: Hafiz’s Persian couplet argues that since sin struck the pure Adam, people cannot credibly claim to be sinless.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r6.anchor: قال الحافظ : جايى كه برق عصيان بر آدم صفى زد

BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r7.claim: The command to Muhammad concerns taking charity from the wealth of those who stayed behind and admitted their sins.
BURSEVI:v3p374#3/r7.anchor: {خذ} يا محمد {من أموالهم} أي : من أموال هؤلاء المتخلفين المعترفين بذنوبهم

BURSEVI:v3p375/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r1.claim: Sadaqa is construed as a circumstantial accusative: take from their wealth in the state of giving charity.

BURSEVI:v3p375/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r2.claim: The charity cleanses them of the stain of having stayed behind.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r2.anchor: {تطهرهم} أي : عما تلطخوا به من أوضار التخلف

BURSEVI:v3p375/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r3.claim: Through the charity and its collection, their good deeds grow and they rise to the ranks of the sincere.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r3.anchor: تنمى بتلك الصدقة وأخذها حسناتهم وترفعهم إلى مراتب المخلصين

BURSEVI:v3p375/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r4.claim: After their repentance and release from bonds, the wrongdoers brought all their wealth and asked the Prophet to give charity for them; he disliked it, then the verse came and he took a third as completion of repentance and expiation for staying behind.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r4.anchor: روي أنه لما حلهم النبي عليه السلام من وثاقهم وتاب الله عليهم راحوا إلى منازلهم وجاؤوا بأموالهم كلها

BURSEVI:v3p375/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r5.claim: On the first account this charity is not obligatory zakat, which is not collected in this manner.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r5.anchor: فهذه الصدقة ليست الصدقة المفروضة فإنها

BURSEVI:v3p375/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375/r6.claim: Another view treats the passage as a new command requiring zakat from affluent Muslims even without a previously mentioned group; most jurists hold this, and sadaqa signals truthful servitude.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r6.anchor: وقيل : هذا كلام مبتدأ نزل لإيجاب أخذ الزكاة من الأغنياء عليه

BURSEVI:v3p375/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r7.speaker: الاختيار
BURSEVI:v3p375/r7.claim: Al-Ikhtiyar says the imam forcibly collects zakat from a refuser and places it where due, citing this verse.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r7.anchor: قال في "الاختيار" : من امتنع عن أداء الزكاة أخذها الإمام كرها

BURSEVI:v3p375/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r8.speaker: الأشباه
BURSEVI:v3p375/r8.claim: Al-Ashbah reports that the relied-upon school position is not to seize zakat by force.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r8.anchor: وفي "الأشباه" المعتمد في المذهب عدم الأخذ كرها

BURSEVI:v3p375/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r9.speaker: المحيط
BURSEVI:v3p375/r9.claim: Al-Muhit says an official should not forcibly take zakat; if taken without consent it does not discharge the duty, so the payer is compelled by imprisonment to pay personally.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r9.anchor: قال في "المحيط" : ومن امتنع من أداء الزكاة فالساعي لا يأخذ منه كرها

BURSEVI:v3p375/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375/r10.speaker: المبسوط
BURSEVI:v3p375/r10.claim: Al-Mabsut’s sounder view is that payments to unjust officials of charity, tithes, jizya, kharaj, levies, or confiscations discharge the owner’s obligation if paid with charitable intent; another view advises repeating payment if the collector knew its nature.
BURSEVI:v3p375/r10.anchor: قال في "المبسوط" : وما يأخذ ظلمة زماننا من الصدقات والعشور والجزية والخراج

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is to pray for their good and blessing and ask forgiveness for them.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r1.anchor: أي ادع لهم بالخير والبركة واستغفر لهم

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r2.claim: The Prophet’s prayers calm their souls and reassure their hearts; sakan is a passive-form noun, like naqd meaning something spent or broken.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r2.anchor: تسكن إليها نفوسهم وتطمئن بها قلوبهم فهو فعل بمعنى مفعول كالنقض بمعنى المنقوض

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r3.claim: God hears their confession and knows their remorse.

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r4.speaker: الكافي
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r4.claim: Al-Kafi cites this verse and the report pray over every righteous and sinful person as evidence that funeral prayer is prescribed.

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r5.claim: One account says Adam was shrouded and embalmed with materials from Paradise, washed and shrouded by angels, and prayed over by an angel leading the angels.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r5.anchor: روي أن آدم عليه السلام لما توفي أتي بحنوط وكفن من الجنة ونزلت الملائكة

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r6.speaker: جبريل
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r6.claim: In another account, Seth asks Gabriel to pray over Adam; Gabriel tells Seth to lead, and Seth prays with thirty takbirs before the burial and lahd.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r6.anchor: وفي رواية : قال ولده شيث لجبريل عليه السلام صل عليه فقال له جبريل تقدم أنت

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r7.claim: The Adam accounts make washing, shrouding, funeral prayer, burial, and lahd ancient religious practices.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r7.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن الغسل والتكفين والصلاة والدفن واللحد من الشرائع القديمة

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r8.claim: The claim that funeral prayer is unique to this community does not contradict ancient precedent: Quraysh need not have known of it, or they would have practiced it.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم صلاة الجنازة من خصائص هذه الأمة ولا منافاة لأنه لا يلزم

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r9.claim: Some say pre-Islamic Arabs washed and shrouded their dead, then the deceased’s guardian stood by the bier, recited virtues, invoked mercy, and buried the body.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r9.anchor: وفي كلام بعضهم كانوا في الجاهلية يغسلون موتاهم وكانوا يكفنونهم ويصلون عليهم

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r10.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r10.claim: When the Prophet reached Medina, Bara ibn Marur had died; the Prophet and companions prayed at his grave with four takbirs. Scholars date the obligation to the first Hijri year.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r10.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام لما قدم المدينة وجد البراء بن معرور رضي الله عنه قد مات

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r11.speaker: القنية
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r11.claim: Al-Qunya states that someone who denies the obligatory status of funeral prayer is an unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r11.anchor: ومن أنكر فرضية صلاة الجنازة كفر كما في "القنية".

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r12.claim: Washing the dead is a communal obligation; intention is not required for the washing’s validity but does discharge the duty for the washer and community, and if everyone omits it all are sinful.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r12.anchor: إن غسل الميت فرض كفاية فإذا تركوا أثموا فبنية الغسل يسقط الفرض عن ذمة الغاسل وغيره

BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r13.claim: The dead become impure at death like other blood-bearing animals, but washing purifies them as an honor; even a body found in water must be washed because people have not performed the commanded act.
BURSEVI:v3p375#2/r13.anchor: وإنما يغسل الميت لأنه يتنجس بالموت كسائر الحيوانات الدموية إلا أنه يطهر بالغسل

RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command concerns repentant men who offered their wealth; taking it completes their repentance like expiation, and it is not obligatory zakat but charity expiating their sin.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن ، وكان يقول ليس المراد من هذه الآية الصدقة الواجبة

RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r3.claim: A second view says zakat was already obligatory; after they repented from missing the expedition, professed Islam sincerely, and offered zakat, the Messenger was ordered to collect it.
RAZI-FULL:v16p140#2/r3.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن الزكوات كانت واجبة عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r1.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r1.claim: A third view, held by most jurists, treats the passage as a new command to collect zakat from the wealthy; they cite it to establish zakat’s obligation and call zakat purification.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r1.anchor: والقول الثالث : أن هذه الآية كلام مبتدأ ، والمقصود منها إيجاب أخذ الزكاة من الأغنياء وعليه أكثر الفقهاء

RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r2.speaker: القائلون بالقول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r2.claim: Those favoring expiatory charity argue that a fresh zakat command would break the coherence with surrounding verses and leave this one unrelated to what precedes and follows.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r2.anchor: احتجوا على صحة قولهم بأن الآيات لا بد وأن تكون منتظمة متناسقة

RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r3.speaker: القائلون بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r3.claim: Defenders of obligatory zakat preserve the link: the men admitted love of wealth had caused their absence, so paying zakat willingly tests whether their repentance is sincere; refusal exposes them as liars.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r3.anchor: فكأنه قيل لهم إنما يظهر صحة قولكم في ادعاء هذه التوبة والندامة لو أخرجتم الزكاة الواجبة

RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r4.claim: Razi prefers obligatory zakat because purification from sin by taking the charity fits only an obligation: sin would result if they failed to pay what was due.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r4.anchor: وهذا إنما يصح لو قلنا إنه لو لم يأخذ تلك الصدقة لحصل الذنب ، وذلك إنما يصح حصوله في الصدقات الواجبة

RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r5.claim: A report says the men offered wealth to seek purification and forgiveness; the Prophet initially said he had no order to take it, then took one-third and left two-thirds after revelation. مِن indicates a portion, and Razi says the report still fits his preferred view because willingness to give optional charity makes willingness to pay obligations more fitting.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141/r5.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآيات فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلث أموالهم ، وترك الثلثين لأنه تعالى قال : { خذ من أموالهم صدقة } ولم يقل خذ أموالهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r1.claim: The command takes a known portion, not an arbitrary amount: the charity's amount and manner were already specified, since even a single grain cannot be the intended minimum.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r1.anchor: القدر المأخوذ بعض تلك الأموال لا كلها إذ مقدار ذلك البعض غير مذكور ههنا بصريح اللفظ

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r2.claim: The specified obligatory charity consists of the prescribed kinds and quantities the Prophet set, such as the camel schedules; paying its monetary value does not discharge it, according to al-Shāfiʿī.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r2.anchor: الصدقة التي بين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هي أنه أمر بأن يؤخذ في خمس وعشرين

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r3.claim: Because the verse says their wealth belongs to them, the poor do not share ownership of the zakat threshold; zakat is a debt on the owner's liability, not a right attached to the asset.

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r4.claim: If an owner delays zakat until the threshold property perishes, the liability remains because the obligation attached to the owner's debt, not to the destroyed property.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r4.anchor: فوجب أن يبقى ذلك الوجوب بعد هلاك النصاب

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r5.claim: The verse's general wording entails zakat on a debtor's wealth and on wealth subject to a guarantee.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r5.anchor: ظاهر هذا العموم يوجب الزكاة في مال المديون

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa holds zakat obligatory only for an adult: purification from sins presupposes the capacity to sin, which children lack.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r6.anchor: وكونها طهرة عن الآثام لا يتقرر إلا حيث يمكن حصول الآثام

RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r7.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī replies that taking zakat from a child's or mad person's property entails its being purifying; absence of one particular cause does not prove the ruling itself absent.
RAZI-FULL:v16p141#2/r7.anchor: لا يلزم من انتفاء سبب معين انتفاء الحكم مطلقا

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r1.claim: One parsing supplies the sense: Take charity from their wealth, O Muḥammad, for you purify them.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r1.anchor: خذ يا محمد من أموالهم صدقة فإنك تطهرهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r2.claim: Another parsing makes the charity itself purifying; charity is called people's dregs, so removing it resembles purification.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r2.anchor: وإنما حسن جعل الصدقة مطهرة لما جاء أن الصدقة أوساخ الناس

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r3.claim: A third parsing treats the tāʾ in both verbs as the second-person pronoun: the collector purifies them by taking charity and sanctifies them through it.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r3.anchor: يجعل التاء في { تطهرهم وتزكيهم } ضمير المخاطب

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports a reading with the form from aṭhara, meaning ṭahhara, and another with تطهرهم jussive as a response to the command.

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r5.claim: The reading transmitted here keeps the yāʾ in both تطهرهم and تزكيهم.

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r6.claim: One view takes tazkiya as a more emphatic form of purification, distinct from the preceding verb.

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r7.claim: Another view glosses tazkiya as growth: God makes the reduction from paying zakat lead to increase.

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r8.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r8.claim: A further view says charity cleanses the donor of sin, while the Messenger raises the donor's standing and praises them when it is delivered to the poor.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r8.anchor: الصدقة تطهرهم عن نجاسة الذنب والمعصية

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r9.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read the prayer as singular; the other readers use the plural, as in Hūd 11:87.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r9.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { ءان } بغير واو وفتح التاء على التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda prefers the singular reading because prayer is more common than prayers and argues that صلوات is a plural of paucity, as in the phrase three or five prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r10.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : والقراءة الأولى أولى لأن الصلاة أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r11.speaker: أبو حاتم
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r11.claim: Abū Ḥātim rejects Abū ʿUbayda's argument: the form صلوات is not restricted to small numbers, as other Qur'anic plural forms show.
RAZI-FULL:v16p142/r11.anchor: قال أبو حاتم : هذا غلط لأن بناء الصلوات ليس للقلة

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r1.speaker: مانعو الزكاة في زمان أبي بكر
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r1.claim: Those who withheld zakat in Abū Bakr's time argued that payment was conditional on the Prophet praying for the payer, so it need be paid only to him.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r1.anchor: احتج مانعو الزكاة في زمان أبي بكر بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī calls that argument weak: other verses make zakat due to meet the poor's need, not because the Prophet's prayer is a condition.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r2.anchor: واعلم أنه ضعيف لأن سائر الآيات دلت على أن الزكاة إنما وجبت دفعا لحاجة الفقير

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r3.claim: Ṣalāt originally means supplication in Arabic; by convention, praying for someone came to mean saying “O God, bless him.”
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r3.anchor: لا شك أن الصلاة في أصل اللغة عبارة عن الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as “pray for them”; al-Shāfiʿī says the imam should pray for a donor, with a formula asking God to reward what was given and bless what remains.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r4.anchor: نقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : معناه ادع لهم

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r5.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r5.claim: Another interpretation says to invoke God's blessing on the donor; the Prophet prayed, “O God, bless the family of Abū Awfā,” when they brought charity.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r5.anchor: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام ، أن آل أبي أوفى لما أتوه بالصدقة قال : ( اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r6.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī reports from al-Kaʿbī that ʿAlī said “peace and blessings upon you” to ʿUmar when he lay shrouded.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r6.anchor: عن الكعبي في ( تفسيره ) أنه قال علي لعمر

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to say that no one should invoke ṣalāt on anyone except the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r7.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال لا تنبغي الصلاة من أحد على أحد إلا في حق النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī's school prohibits the formula “God's blessings upon him” or “peace and blessings upon him” for anyone except the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r8.anchor: أن أصحابنا يمنعون من ذكر صلوات الله عليه وعليه الصلاة والسلام إلا في حق الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r9.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r9.claim: The Shīʿa use the formula for ʿAlī and his descendants, arguing that the Qur'an permits it for zakat payers and that returning “peace be upon you” is accepted; they ask why it should be denied to ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn.

RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r10.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r10.claim: Al-Qāḍī allows the formula for the Prophet, citing the taught blessing on Muḥammad and his family; because no member of that family is a prophet, it includes ʿAlī, as with Abraham's family.
RAZI-FULL:v16p143/r10.anchor: قال القاضي : إنه جائز في حق الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r1.claim: One analysis allows an indefinite noun to be a subject when it is qualified: سلام means complete, perfect peace, so it can stand as subject and عليكم is its predicate; the argument cites 2:221 and 2:96.

RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p144/r2.claim: Alternatively, عليكم qualifies سلام, making سلام عليكم a full subject with an omitted predicate; deleting that predicate can heighten awe and grandeur.

RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh explains the reply's reversed order, وعليكم السلام, by saying speakers put first what matters most to them; the reply thus signals great concern for the greeter.
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r1.anchor: والسبب فيه ما قاله سيبويه أنهم يقدمون الأهم والذي هم بشأنه أعنى

RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r2.claim: The reply also implies restriction: if the greeter sent peace to me, I return more by making peace exclusive to them, fulfilling 4:86.
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r2.anchor: فكأنه يقول إن كنت قد أوصلت السلام إلي

RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī says indefinite سلام عليك is fuller than definite السلام عليك because the indefinite suggests perfect qualities beyond the bare essence; al-Shāfiʿī therefore chose the indefinite in the tashahhud.
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r3.anchor: اختار الشافعي رحمه الله في قراءة التشهد

RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī supports the distinction by observing that God's peace is generally indefinite, while definite السلام appears in prophetic speech; he notes Yahya as an exception because his greeting is from God.
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r4.anchor: من الله تعالى ورد على سبيل التنكير

RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r5.claim: The world is full of harms, and al-Rāzī argues animal nature inclines to evil: humans and animals instinctively flee an unknown approaching creature, which they would not do if goodness were their natural expectation.
RAZI-FULL:v16p144#2/r5.anchor: علمنا أن الأصل في الحيوان هو الشر

RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī gives three reasons preventing harm matters more than bringing benefit: it preserves the baseline, universal good is impossible while restraint is possible, and harm causes pain whereas lack of added good leaves safety.
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r1.anchor: أن دفع الشر أهم من إيصال الخير

RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r2.claim: Since the world is harmful and creatures are disposed to harm, a greeting begins with peace to reassure the other person of safety and security.
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r2.anchor: كان أهم المهمات أن يعرفه أنه منه في السلامة

RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r3.claim: The plural greeting suits a person accompanied by guardian angels, as well as several classes of human spirits, corresponding upper spirits that inspire them, and similar disembodied spirits that assist toward good or evil.
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى تسليم هذا الشخص المخصوص على جميع الأرواح

RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r4.claim: When virtuous, knowledgeable human spirits become strongly connected, their lights reflect into one another like facing mirrors; this explains a student's etiquette of praising God, angels, and prophets, praying for the teacher, then reading to receive spiritual illumination.
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r4.anchor: فالأدب أن يبدأ بحمد الله والثناء على الملائكة الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī concludes that saying سلام عليكم creates a strong spiritual bond, producing congruence between spirits and reciprocal reflection of their lights.
RAZI-FULL:v16p145/r5.anchor: حدث بينهما تعلق شديد ، وحصل بسبب ذلك التعلق تطابق الأرواح وتعاكس الأنوار

IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r5.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r5.claim: The passage next commands taking alms from them to purify and cleanse them.
IBNHISHAM:v2p553#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها 9: 103 إلى آخر القصة

QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r1.claim: After someone said he had not been ordered to take anything from their wealth, God revealed the command to take alms from their property.
QURTUBI-FULL:9:102/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى { خذ من أموالهم صدقة } الآية

TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r7.claim: The Prophet took one third of their wealth and left two thirds because the command says take from their wealth, not take all of it.
TABRISI:9:101-102#3/r7.anchor: وفي جميع الأقوال أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلث أموالهم وترك الثلثين
